title: Owner Story & Credentials
our_text:
# Owner Story & Credentials

Section prompt for the about/trust block on an S1 homepage, sitting after the services grid and before reviews. For most 1–9 employee local businesses this is the differentiator ad spend cannot buy: a real person, their credentials, and proof they'll show up. Done means a visitor can name who they'd be hiring and what backs that person up, in under ten seconds.

## Structure

1. Photograph — owner or team, on-site or at work, not a studio headshot unless supplied.
2. Origin story — two to four sentences on who runs the business and why.
3. Credential list — licences, insurance, certifications, affiliations, each a short labelled item.
4. Guarantee statement (optional) — one sentence on what the client promises if something goes wrong.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile (<640px): photograph above text, single column, full-width image at a fixed aspect ratio.
Tablet (640–1023px): two-column split, photograph left or right per the client's reading-order preference.
Desktop (≥1024px): same split, wider gutter; credential list moves to a two-column sub-grid past four items.
The photograph column reserves its aspect-ratio box (`aspect-ratio: 4/5` or client-supplied ratio) before the image loads, so nothing reflows once it arrives.

## Typography

Section heading: role "display-sm", one step below the page H1.
Origin story: role "body", 1rem–1.125rem, line length 50–75 characters, line-height 1.6.
Credential items: role "label", 0.875rem–1rem, medium weight for the name, regular weight for its qualifier (jurisdiction, number, expiry).

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` — section background. `--ink` — story/credential text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`. `--muted` — qualifiers (licence numbers, dates), 4.5:1, never the sole carrier of meaning. `--border` — mobile divider, 3:1. `--accent` — credential icon or guarantee rule, 3:1.

## Components

**AboutPhoto** — fixed-aspect image container. Default: loaded image. Loading: aspect-ratio box, neutral fill, no spinner. Error: neutral placeholder box; the intended alt text still describes what should be there.

**CredentialList** — unordered list, one item per credential. Default: label plus qualifier, optional small decorative icon (`aria-hidden`). Not interactive unless a credential links to a verifying body, in which case it follows link states: default, hover (underline, ≤150ms), focus-visible (visible outline).

**GuaranteeCallout** — optional single-sentence block, visually distinct via an `--accent` rule, not styled as a button.

## Content slots

- `photo`: real photograph of the owner or team. Placeholder: `[Owner/team photo — client to supply]`.
- `story`: 2–4 sentences, plain language, first or third person per client preference.
- `credentials[]`: each `{ label, qualifier? }`, e.g. `{ label: "Licensed & Insured", qualifier: "State Lic. #XXXXXX" }`. Placeholder: `[Licence number — client to supply]`, never fabricated.
- `guarantee`: one sentence, optional, only if the client actually offers one.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: micro. Credential-link hover/focus transitions ≤150ms, color or underline only. No image reveal animation, no parallax, no counter-up on years-in-business. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the transition entirely rather than shortening it.

## Accessibility

- Photograph has a real, specific `alt` (e.g. "Maria Chen, owner, standing in front of a service van"), never "photo" or empty when the image carries content.
- Section heading is a sibling of the services grid's heading, both one level below the page H1.
- Credential list is a true `<ul>`/`<li>` so assistive tech announces item count.
- Any credential that links out has a minimum 44×44px hit target and a visible focus ring ≥2px.
- Qualifier text (licence numbers) is never conveyed by color alone.

## Performance

The photograph is a likely LCP candidate if the hero above it is lightweight — `loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"` only when genuinely above the fold, otherwise `loading="lazy"`. Explicit `width`/`height` (or `aspect-ratio`) always, to prevent shift.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: credentials lead with manufacturer certifications alongside licence/insurance.
- Salon/spa: photograph often becomes a stylist/therapist grid, not a single owner photo.
- Fitness: origin story emphasizes trainer certifications over business licensing.
- Cleaning: bonding/insurance status is the load-bearing credential — list it first.

## Acceptance checks

1. Photograph renders in a reserved aspect-ratio box with zero layout shift on load.
2. Origin story is 2–4 sentences, no filler padding.
3. Every credential has a real or explicitly placeholdered qualifier — no fabricated licence numbers.
4. Guarantee callout appears only when client-supplied; the section works without it.
5. Photo `alt` text is specific, not generic.
6. All credential-list text meets 4.5:1 contrast against `--surface`.

title: Booking Adapter
our_text:
# Booking Adapter

An accessible entry point to book, wrapping a third-party scheduler (Calendly-class) behind our own trigger, with a native form fallback so booking never fully depends on a third-party script. Done means a visitor can always request an appointment, whether the embed loads or not.

## Structure
- Trigger — a real button, not a link, opening the scheduler.
- Scheduler surface — the third-party embed (iframe or widget script), loaded on demand.
- Fallback form — native HTML form (name, phone, service, date/time range, notes) shown when the embed fails, is blocked, or JS is unavailable.
- Confirmation state — shown after either path succeeds.

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<768px): trigger is full-width or paired with the call button; scheduler or fallback opens as a full-screen sheet. Tablet/desktop (≥768px): a centered modal (max-width ~560px) or an inline panel, depending on placement. The fallback form stacks single-column at every width — never multi-column.

## Typography
Inherits the page's type scale. Labels sit at label size (14–16px), always visible above the field, never placeholder-only. Confirmation heading uses the page's h2 scale.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface` (modal/panel background, 4.5:1 against `--ink`); `--ink` (body and label text); `--accent` (trigger and focus ring, 3:1 against the adjacent surface); `--border` (field outlines, 3:1 against `--surface`); `--error` (validation state, 4.5:1 against `--surface`, always paired with an icon and text, never colour alone).

## Components
- **Trigger button** — states: default, hover, focus-visible (never suppressed), active, disabled (embed loading), loading (spinner if load exceeds ~300ms).
- **Scheduler embed** — states: loading (skeleton, not blank), loaded, blocked/error (ad-blocker, script failure, timeout after ~5s), success (advances to confirmation).
- **Fallback form** — states: default, focus-visible per field, invalid (message tied to field via `aria-describedby`), submitting, submit error, success.
- **Confirmation** — two copy-distinct variants: booked-via-embed, and booked-via-fallback (sets the expectation "we'll confirm by phone or text," since a form submission holds no live calendar slot).

## Content slots
- Scheduler provider and embed URL — [Client-supplied].
- Fallback form's service list — [Client-supplied, matches the services grid].
- Confirmation copy for both paths — [Client-supplied or Zero Sum default; must state the actual next step].
- No availability window, price or hold is ever invented — shown only what the provider or client has confirmed.

## Interaction & motion
Micro budget: modal/sheet open and trigger state changes ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. No scroll-jacking, no embed autoplay. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the open/close transition entirely — no animation, not a shortened one.

## Accessibility
Trigger and fallback fields are real form controls, never a `<div>` with a click handler. The modal traps focus while open, returns focus to the trigger on close, and closes on Escape. Every field has a programmatic `<label>`; errors use `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, announced via `aria-live="polite"`. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Focus-visible meets 3:1 contrast. Keyboard path: Tab to trigger → Enter/Space opens → Tab cycles fields in order → Escape closes and returns focus.

## Performance
The third-party embed script loads only on trigger interaction (or `/booking` route load) — never part of the initial bundle. The fallback form is server-rendered and works with zero JavaScript. This component is never the page's LCP element. Reserve space for the embed at its expected height with a skeleton, so resolving it causes no layout shift.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: fallback form includes an "emergency" flag routing to a phone call instead of a scheduled booking.
- Salon/spa: scheduler should support service-plus-stylist selection where the provider allows it; otherwise capture "preferred stylist" as a fallback field.
- Fitness studio: booking maps to a class or trial session, not an open slot — label the trigger and confirmation accordingly.
- Cleaning service: fallback form captures property size and frequency alongside date, since these drive the quote.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] The trigger is a real `<button>`, operable by keyboard alone.
- [ ] The fallback form renders and submits successfully with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] A simulated embed block shows the fallback within ~5 seconds, not a blank panel.
- [ ] The third-party script is absent from the initial page load and loads only on interaction.
- [ ] The modal traps and returns focus correctly, and Escape closes it.
- [ ] Every fallback field has an associated label and an error message tied via `aria-describedby`.
- [ ] Reduced motion removes the open/close transition rather than shortening it.
- [ ] No confirmation copy implies a guarantee the provider has not actually made.

title: Cleaning Service Site
our_text:
# Cleaning Service Site

Complete homepage for a residential or commercial cleaning company. The job is
converting a visitor into a quote request fast — most compare three companies in
one sitting, so the instant quote estimator is the page's real product. Done means
a visitor gets a realistic price range in under a minute and knows what happens
next when a human takes over.

## Structure

1. Header — logo, nav (Services, Pricing, About, Reviews, Contact), tap-to-call
   phone, primary "Get Instant Quote" button.
2. Hero — what's cleaned and area served, call CTA, quote CTA, one photo of real
   staff or work.
3. Proof strip — bonded, insured, background-checked staff, years, rating.
4. Instant quote estimator — property type/size and frequency in, price range and
   lead form out.
5. Recurring plans — one-time, weekly, biweekly, monthly, framed by savings.
6. Services list — standard, deep, move-in/out, office/commercial.
7. About/trust — team, guarantee, satisfaction policy.
8. Reviews — third-party rating with quotes.
9. Map, hours (incl. holiday overrides), contact form, booking entry.
10. Footer — NAP, service-area list, bonding/insurance detail, legal.

## Layout & responsive

Single column under 640px. 768px+: proof strip becomes 4 columns, plans move to a
4-column row, services become 2 columns. Estimator is single-column at every
width, even desktop — sequential questions must not compete for attention. Sticky
call/quote bar under 768px only, never overlapping estimator fields.

## Typography

Display/body/label, modular scale 1.25. Display 2.5rem mobile → 3.5rem desktop,
body 1rem/1.6, label 0.875rem uppercase for plan names and step indicators. Body
line length ~70ch. Estimator questions are body weight, not headings; heading
order h1 → h2 per section → h3 per card or step.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--surface-raised` (cards, estimator panel), `--ink` (4.5:1),
`--accent` (CTAs, active step, 3:1), `--muted` (price-range disclaimer, still
4.5:1 — it carries real information), `--border` (3:1). All client-set; no brand
colour named.

## Components

**InstantQuoteEstimator** — steps: property type, size/room count, frequency,
add-ons, contact details. States: default, focus-visible, step validation error
(`aria-describedby`), calculating (explicit, not spinner-only), result (price
range labelled an estimate), result unavailable (falls back to "we'll call you"),
submitting, success (states response time/channel), error (retry, keeps answers).
**RecurringPlanCard** — frequency, savings framing, features, CTA that pre-fills
the estimator. States: default, hover, focus-visible, "most requested".
**ProofStripItem** — bonded/insured/background-checked badges. Static only.
**ReviewsBlock** — aggregate rating and quotes, link to source. States: default,
loading (skeleton), empty (no fabricated reviews), blocked (falls back to the
client-supplied static rating).

## Content slots

Company name, area served, hero photo (real, ≤200KB). Bonding/insurance detail,
years (client-verified). Estimator logic: property types, size bands, frequency
options, add-ons, price-per-band supplied by the client (formula or lookup table,
not invented). Plans: frequency, savings amount, 3–5 bullets. Reviews: `[Client
review — 1–2 sentences]`, obviously fake. Post-quote copy: confirmation channel
and response-time commitment.

## Interaction & motion

Micro: hover/focus-visible on buttons, cards, step transitions, ≤150ms, opacity/
transform only. Steps swap content, never slide or carousel. Reduced-motion sets
all durations to 0. No autoplay crew video, no scroll-triggered reveals.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible focus ring everywhere, including estimator controls and
plan CTAs. Logical heading order. Every field labelled, errors tied via
`aria-describedby` and announced on step advance. Touch targets ≥44×44px.
Contrast 4.5:1 body/price text, 3:1 large text and borders. Keyboard path: nav →
hero CTAs → estimator steps (change announced via a live region) → plan cards →
reviews → contact form → footer. No trap in the estimator; a visible back
control corrects earlier answers.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading or photo — explicit width/height,
`fetchpriority="high"`, no lazy-load. Estimator runs client-side, no third-party
dependency, off any critical-path block. Service/plan images `loading="lazy"`
with explicit dimensions. Webfonts use `font-display: swap` with matched
fallback metrics. Map embed loads on interaction, requests consent before any
tracking cookie.

## Vertical adaptation

- Instant quote estimator replaces the generic S1 contact block as the primary
  conversion mechanism — a genuinely new component; its accessibility (step
  announcement, error recovery, no dead end) is the hardest part of this build.
- Proof strip leads with bonded/insured/background-checked, not licence numbers
  — cleaners work inside a client's home or office, so vetting is the signal.
- Recurring plans replace a flat services grid: the product is a cleaning
  cadence, and price is always a range, never false-precision.
- Every quote result names the human handoff (call/text, stated window) — the
  flow must never read as a final, binding price.
- Imagery is real staff and completed work (consent on file), never an actual
  client's home or stock cleaning photos.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Hero shows area served, one real photo, call and quote CTAs above the fold
      at 360px.
- [ ] Estimator is single-column at every breakpoint, never multi-column.
- [ ] Validation error, calculating, result, result-unavailable, submit-error
      states are all implemented.
- [ ] Estimator result is labelled an estimate and states the next human contact
      step and timing.
- [ ] Step changes announce via a live region; a visible back control exists at
      every step.
- [ ] All motion ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, removed under reduced-motion.
- [ ] Hero image has explicit dimensions and `fetchpriority="high"`; no font-swap
      CLS.
- [ ] Every colour is a semantic token with a stated contrast ratio.
- [ ] Reviews are marked client-supplied, visibly fake; reviews block has a
      defined blocked/empty state.
- [ ] Full keyboard path header-to-footer reaches every element, including every
      estimator step, no trap.

title: Fitness Studio Site
our_text:
# Fitness Studio Site

Complete homepage for an independent gym or studio: CrossFit box, yoga or Pilates
studio, boxing gym, boutique cycling. The job is converting a visitor into a
free-trial signup or booked class, using a schedule they trust is current. Done
means a stranger finds a class that fits their week and books it in under a minute
on a phone.

## Structure

1. Header — nav (Schedule, Membership, Trainers, About, Contact), tap-to-call
   phone, primary "Book a Free Trial" button.
2. Hero — studio type, area served, one action photo, trial CTA, schedule CTA.
3. Proof strip — certifying bodies, years, member count, review rating.
4. Class schedule — the week's classes, filterable by day and type.
5. Membership tiers — comparison table, drop-in vs recurring.
6. Trainer profiles — grid with certifications.
7. About/studio story — space, equipment, guarantee.
8. Reviews — third-party rating with quotes.
9. Free-trial signup — short form, what happens next.
10. Map, hours (incl. holiday overrides), contact.
11. Footer — NAP, cancellation policy, social, legal.

## Layout & responsive

Single column under 640px. 768px+: proof strip becomes 4 columns, tiers move from
stacked cards to a 3-column grid, trainers go 2- then 3-column at 1024px.
Schedule reflows from a day-by-day accordion (mobile) to a 7-column table
(desktop, ≥1024px) — never an image or iframe. Sticky call/book bar under 768px
only.

## Typography

Display/body/label, scale 1.25. Display 2.5rem mobile → 3.5rem desktop, body
1rem/1.6, label 0.875rem uppercase for schedule headers and tier names. Line
length ~70ch. Class/trainer names are labels, not headings; order h1 → h2 per
section → h3 per card.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--surface-raised` (cards, schedule), `--ink` (4.5:1), `--accent`
(CTAs, active-day indicator, 3:1), `--muted` (schedule metadata, 4.5:1 — it is
information, not decoration), `--border` (3:1). Client-set; no brand colour named.

## Components

**ClassScheduleTable** — day tabs or 7 columns; slot shows class, time, duration,
instructor, level. States: default, hover/focus-visible, full (waitlist link),
cancelled (struck through, reason shown), loading (skeleton), empty day, stale
("last updated" stamp linking to the live booking system).
**MembershipTierCard** — name, price, cadence, features, CTA. States: default,
hover, focus-visible, "most popular", sold-out.
**TrainerCard** — photo, name, certifications, specialty, bio. States: default,
hover, focus-visible, missing-photo fallback (initials, no layout shift).
**FreeTrialForm** — name, contact, preferred class/day, consent. States: default,
focus-visible, inline error (`aria-describedby`), submitting, success, error.

## Content slots

Studio name, area served, hero photo (real, ≤200KB). Certifications, years.
Weekly class list: name, day, time, duration, level, instructor, capacity —
client-fed, kept current. Tiers: name, price, cadence, 3–6 bullets. Trainers:
photo, name, certifications, 1–2 sentence bio. Reviews: `[Client review — 1–2
sentences]`, obviously fake. Trial-form copy: next steps, response time.

## Interaction & motion

Micro: hover/focus-visible on buttons, cards, schedule slots, ≤150ms, opacity/
transform only. Day changes swap content, never slide. Reduced-motion sets all
durations to 0. No autoplay video, no scroll-triggered reveals.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible focus ring everywhere, including schedule slots and tier
CTAs. Logical heading order. Controls labelled, errors tied via
`aria-describedby` and announced. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Contrast 4.5:1 body/
schedule text, 3:1 large text and borders. Keyboard path: nav → hero → schedule
tabs → slot links → tier CTAs → trainer cards → trial form → footer, no trap.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading or photo — explicit width/height,
`fetchpriority="high"`, no lazy-load. Schedule renders server-side first (cached
snapshot), hydrates; never blocks first paint on a third-party feed. Trainer/
class images `loading="lazy"` with explicit dimensions. Webfonts use
`font-display: swap` with matched fallback metrics. No render-blocking booking
script above the fold.

## Vertical adaptation

- Primary action shifts from S1's generic "call or book" to book-first: people
  pick a class time, not a business to call. Phone stays present, secondary.
- Class schedule is a component the generic skeleton lacks; staleness, not
  layout, is the failure mode to design against.
- Proof strip leads with certifying bodies and trainer credentials, not licence
  numbers — trust here is about who teaches.
- Membership tiers replace a flat services grid: pricing is a plan, not a
  per-job estimate.
- Imagery is real action shots, never stock gym photography.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Hero shows area served, one real photo, trial and schedule CTAs above the
      fold at 360px.
- [ ] Schedule is accordion under 768px, a table at 1024px+, never image/iframe.
- [ ] Full, cancelled, empty-day, and stale schedule states are all implemented.
- [ ] Membership table is markup-accessible, not an image; trial-form errors are
      tied to their field and announced.
- [ ] All motion ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, removed under reduced-motion;
      hero image has explicit dimensions and `fetchpriority="high"`, no font-swap
      CLS.
- [ ] Every colour is a semantic token with a stated contrast ratio.
- [ ] Reviews and trainer bios are marked client-supplied, visibly fake.
- [ ] Full keyboard path header-to-footer reaches every element, no trap.

title: Local Business Footer
our_text:
# Local Business Footer

The page's final trust signal and the canonical source for NAP-consistent business facts, repeated verbatim from the header and the schema. Done means every page ends in the same footer, and its facts never drift from the schema markup and Google Business Profile.

## Structure
- Business identity — name, logo mark (optional), one-line tagline.
- NAP block — address, phone, hours including holiday overrides.
- Service area — list of cities or regions served.
- Licence & insurance — licence numbers, bonding/insurance statement.
- Navigation — secondary links (services, about, reviews, contact), lighter-weight than the primary nav.
- Social links — icon links to verified profiles only.
- Legal — privacy policy, terms, and accessibility statement links.

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<640px): single column, stacked as above. Tablet (640–1024px): two columns (identity+NAP paired, nav+legal paired). Desktop (≥1024px): three to four columns (identity, NAP, service area, legal-and-social). Column count changes across breakpoints; content order within each column does not.

## Typography
Footer body sits one step below the page's base body size on the modular scale (for example, base × 0.875). Column headings sit at label scale, differentiated by weight or case rather than size, so they never compete with page content. Line length is capped at roughly 40 characters per column on desktop.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface` (footer background, typically a distinct step from the page background); `--ink` (footer text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`); `--muted` (tagline/hours text — muted is a role, not a licence to drop below 4.5:1); `--accent` (link hover/focus, 3:1 against `--surface`); `--border` (column dividers, 3:1 minimum).

## Components
- **NAP block** — static text with one interactive element, a "get directions" link, which carries default, hover and focus-visible states.
- **Hours list** — a default row per day, plus a distinct "closed today" or holiday-override row when one applies, styled by weight or label — never by colour alone.
- **Social links** — icon buttons with default, hover and focus-visible states, each carrying a visible focus outline and an accessible name naming the platform.
- **Legal nav** — plain text links with default, hover, focus-visible and visited states (browser default visited styling is acceptable).

## Content slots
- Legal name, address, phone — [Client-supplied; character-identical to the LocalBusiness schema and Google Business Profile].
- Hours including named holidays — [Client-supplied].
- Licence numbers and insurance statement — [Client-supplied, verifiable].
- Service-area list — [Client-supplied].
- Social profile URLs — [Client-supplied, verified only; omit platforms the business doesn't use].

## Interaction & motion
Static budget: link hover/focus colour or underline change only, ≤150ms if any transition is used at all. No entrance animation on scroll into view. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes any hover transition and applies the end state instantly.

## Accessibility
The footer is a `<footer>` landmark, with its heading one level below the page's last content heading and never skipping a level. Every icon-only social link carries an accessible name (`aria-label="Visit us on Instagram"`). Link and body text meet 4.5:1 contrast; column dividers meet 3:1. Touch targets, including icon links, are ≥44×44px with spacing sufficient to prevent mis-taps. Keyboard path: Tab moves through footer links in visual column order, each with a visible focus outline.

## Performance
The footer is static, server-rendered markup — no client component, no fetch. It adds no web font and no layout shift, inheriting the page's already-loaded font stack. It is never an LCP candidate and nothing in it is render-blocking.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: add an emergency/24-hour line in the NAP block, styled distinctly but without motion.
- Salon/spa: service-area list is often replaced or supplemented with a "book by appointment" note if walk-ins aren't accepted.
- Fitness studio: add a link to the class schedule and membership terms alongside the standard legal links.
- Cleaning service: lead with the bonding/insurance statement over licence numbers if unlicensed in its jurisdiction.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Name, address, phone and hours match the LocalBusiness schema and header exactly, character for character.
- [ ] The footer is wrapped in a `<footer>` landmark with correct heading hierarchy.
- [ ] Every icon-only link has a programmatic accessible name.
- [ ] All text meets 4.5:1 contrast; dividers and boundaries meet 3:1.
- [ ] Touch targets are ≥44×44px with no overlapping hit areas.
- [ ] The footer renders with identical content and order when JavaScript is disabled.
- [ ] No animation plays on scroll into view, and reduced motion removes hover transitions.
- [ ] Social links point only to profiles the client actually maintains.

title: Local Service Hero
our_text:
# Local Service Hero

The above-the-fold opener for the S1 skeleton — the first region a visitor
sees on `/`. Its job is to answer three questions in under two seconds: what
does this business do, does it serve my area, and how do I reach it right now.
Done looks like a visitor on a phone, in sunlight, tapping the phone number
without hunting for it.

## Structure

1. Eyebrow/badge naming the trade (optional, one line).
2. `h1` headline: what the business does, in plain language, not a slogan.
3. One-sentence subhead naming the service area.
4. Primary control: tap-to-call phone number, styled as a button.
5. Secondary CTA: "Book" or "Get a quote," linking to `/booking`.
6. One photograph of real work or the premises.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile (`<640px`): single column, photo above text, phone button full-width
and reachable without scrolling past headline+subhead. Tablet
(`640–1024px`): photo and text side by side, 45/55 split. Desktop
(`>1024px`): same split, max width 1280px, 96–128px vertical padding. The
phone button never wraps its label or number at any width.

## Typography

Headline: display role, 36–48px by breakpoint, semibold, capped near 20 words.
Subhead: body role, 18–20px, one sentence, ≤75ch. Phone number and CTA labels:
label role, 16–18px, medium weight, never smaller than body text.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`/`--ink` for headline/subhead, ≥4.5:1. `--accent` for the phone
button and secondary CTA, ≥3:1 against `--surface` and against the button's
own text. `--border` for any photo edge. `--focus-ring` visible on both
controls at ≥3:1. No hardcoded colours or brand names — maps onto the
client's palette.

## Components

**Phone button**: `tel:` link styled as a filled or high-contrast outline
button, ≥44×44px hit area, digits always visible as text, icon optional and
never icon-only. States: default, hover, focus-visible, active. **Secondary
CTA**: standard button/link, same size floor, same state set. **Hero
photograph**: fixed-aspect container reserved at build time so it never
shifts layout; states are loading (placeholder matching final size) and
loaded — no error state beyond a solid `--surface` fallback with alt text
intact.

## Content slots

Headline copy, subhead/service-area copy, phone number, CTA label, hero
photograph (real work or premises only — never a stock hero video or generic
stock photo). Placeholders are marked obviously: `[Business does X — one
sentence]`, `[Service area, e.g. "Serving Denver Metro"]`, `[Real work photo —
client to supply, min 1600px wide]`.

## Interaction & motion

Avoid by default. Hover and focus-visible states on the two buttons only,
≤150ms, opacity/transform only. No entrance animation on load, no parallax on
the photograph, no autoplaying video background under any circumstance.
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets all transition durations to 0ms.

## Accessibility

`h1` is the headline, and the only `h1` on the page. Phone button's accessible
name includes the full number (e.g. "Call (555) 123-4567"), not just an icon.
Both controls meet the 44×44px floor and show a focus indicator ≥3:1.
Headline/subhead meet 4.5:1 contrast at every breakpoint; if text ever
overlaps the photo, it sits on a solid `--surface` panel instead of relying on
image contrast. Keyboard path: header → phone button → secondary CTA → next
region.

## Performance

The hero photograph is the LCP element: `fetchpriority="high"`, no
`loading="lazy"`, explicit width/height, responsive `srcset` sized to the
layout above. Headline is real text, not text-in-image, so it never waits on
the photo. Fallback font stack matches the loaded webfont's metrics so no
swap causes reflow.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: subhead adds emergency/24-hour framing; photo is a technician or
  truck on a real job.
- Salon/spa: secondary CTA reads "Book an appointment"; photo is the space or
  a finished style, never a stock model.
- Fitness: secondary CTA reads "Start a free trial"; photo is the studio
  floor or a class in session.
- Cleaning: secondary CTA reads "Get an instant quote"; subhead names
  residential/commercial scope.
- Phone-first framing holds across all four; only copy and photo subject
  shift.

## Acceptance checks

1. Exactly one `h1` renders, and it states what the business does.
2. Phone number renders as a real `tel:` link with the number in its
   accessible name.
3. Hero photograph is a real work/premises image, never stock or video.
4. Hero photograph is the identified LCP element with explicit dimensions.
5. No motion exceeds 150ms or animates a property outside opacity/transform.
6. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all hero transitions.
7. Any text over the photograph meets 4.5:1 contrast or sits on a solid
   panel.
8. Both CTAs meet the 44×44px touch-target minimum on mobile.
9. Layout holds without shift at 360px viewport width.

title: HVAC Contractor Site
our_text:
# HVAC Contractor Site

Complete homepage for a residential HVAC contractor: 1–9 technicians, heating and
cooling repair, installation, and maintenance plans. The job is to turn a homeowner
with a broken system into a call within seconds. Done means licensing and
manufacturer standing are visible at a glance, after-hours availability is stated
plainly, and the phone number is reachable from every screen.

## Structure

1. Header — logo, service area, tap-to-call phone, nav, "Book service".
2. Emergency banner — 24/7 availability strip, own call link.
3. Hero — services, area, dual CTA (call now / schedule), one real photo.
4. Proof strip — licence, insurance, years, certifications, rating.
5. Services grid — heating/cooling repair, install/replace, maintenance, air quality, ductwork.
6. Financing & maintenance plans.
7. About/trust — owner or lead tech story, certified-technician claim, dealer badges.
8. Reviews.
9. Service area — map plus towns/zip codes.
10. Contact & booking block.
11. Footer.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile 360–767px: single column, sticky call bar docked bottom, banner full-width under header. Tablet 768–1023px: services grid becomes 2 columns. Desktop 1024px+: grid 3 columns, hero splits copy/image 50–50. Banner never disappears; below 400px it collapses to icon plus tap target, label kept for assistive tech.

## Typography

Roles: display, body, label, and a `tel-display` role one step above body on a 1.25 modular scale, so the phone number reads as a control. Body line length 45–75ch. Headings are sequential; labels never mimic headings.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--ink` (4.5:1), `--accent` (phone and primary CTAs, 3:1 against surface), `--muted`, `--border`, `--urgent` for the banner — still 3:1 against its own background. All client-set; none prescribed here.

## Components

**Header/Nav** — default, scrolled, focus-visible. **EmergencyBanner** — default, dismissed-for-session, reduced-motion. **Hero** — photo skeleton, error fallback. **ServiceCard** — default, hover, focus-visible, skeleton, empty (no detail page — link disabled). **ProofStrip** — static. **FinancingBlock** — default and "unavailable" if dropped. **ReviewsSection** — loading, populated, empty, blocked (static aggregate). **StickyCallBar** — mobile only, dismissible, never covers a focused field. **Footer** — static.

## Content slots

Business name, phone, licence number, insurer/policy status, years in business, manufacturer logos `[Manufacturer certification — client logo]`, service-area town/zip list, financing partner name and disclosure text, review platform and rating, testimonials `[Client testimonial — 2 sentences]`, real job photos, hours with an after-hours line.

## Interaction & motion

Micro budget: hover/focus feedback only, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. The banner never blinks or auto-animates — that reads as spam, not urgency. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all transition. No scrolljacking, no WebGL, no autoplay video.

## Accessibility

Phone numbers are real `tel:` links, minimum 44×44px. The banner announces once via `aria-live="polite"` on load, not on every scroll. Keyboard path: header → banner → hero → services → footer, visible focus rings throughout. Form controls carry labels and programmatic error association. Contrast: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI boundaries.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading plus phone number, or the hero photo — name whichever the build produces. Images ship explicit width/height and `loading="lazy"` except the LCP image, which gets `fetchpriority="high"`. Webfonts use `font-display: swap` with matched fallback metrics. Map embed and financing widget load deferred, never above the fold before consent.

## Vertical adaptation

- Emergency banner is new — no other S1 vertical needs a persistent 24/7 layer; HVAC failure is time-critical, a haircut or cleaning visit is not.
- Proof strip adds manufacturer dealer badges, since brand-authorized status drives replacement decisions.
- Financing is a dedicated region — replacement jobs run to thousands of dollars.
- Service area needs listed towns/zip codes, not just a city name, since dispatch radius is checked first.
- Hero carries a seasonal-urgency slot `[Seasonal callout]`, since "furnace out" and "AC down" alternate by month.

## Acceptance checks

- Phone number is a working `tel:` link in header, hero, banner, and sticky bar.
- Emergency banner is present on load, keyboard-reachable, with no looping animation.
- Services grid shows equal-height cards regardless of copy length; whole card is one link.
- Financing block renders only when the client supplies content, never left empty.
- Manufacturer logos carry client-supplied alt text, never a bare "certified" label.
- Reviews section shows the static rating when the widget is blocked.
- All interactive elements meet 44×44px and show a visible focus ring.
- Contrast of `--urgent` against its background is 3:1 or better.

title: LocalBusiness Schema Pack
our_text:
# LocalBusiness Schema Pack

A structured-data module for local service sites: it injects machine-readable business facts so search engines and AI assistants surface accurate name, address, phone, hours, service area and review data. Covers single- and multi-location businesses. Done means every block validates and describes only content the visitor can actually see on the page.

## Structure
- LocalBusiness JSON-LD (or the most specific subtype) — one block per physical location, rendered server-side.
- Service JSON-LD — one block per service, on that service's detail page, linked to the parent by `@id`.
- FAQPage JSON-LD — one block only on pages with a matching, visible FAQ accordion.
- AggregateRating/Review nodes — nested inside the LocalBusiness node, sourced from the reviews rendered on the page.

## Layout & responsive
No visual surface. A `<script type="application/ld+json">` block injected server-side; identical at every breakpoint, never reflows the page.

## Typography
Not applicable — the module produces no visible type.

## Colour & tokens
Not applicable — the module produces no visible colour.

## Components
- **LocalBusiness node.** Required: `@type` (most specific subtype — `Plumber`, `HVACBusiness` — else `LocalBusiness`), `name`, `address`, `geo`, `telephone`, `url`, `openingHoursSpecification` (holiday overrides as separate exceptions), `areaServed`, `priceRange`. Recommended: `image`, `sameAs`.
- **Multi-location.** One node per location, its own `@id` (canonical URL + `#business`), address and geo. Never merge locations into one node with a combined area.
- **AggregateRating.** `ratingValue`, `reviewCount`, `bestRating`/`worstRating` — generated from the same source as the visible rating, never a static figure.
- **Service node.** `serviceType`, `provider` (LocalBusiness `@id`), `areaServed`, `offers` only when a price is published.
- **FAQPage node.** `mainEntity` pairs generated from the visible accordion, not authored separately.

Example (single location, abbreviated):

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "HVACBusiness",
  "@id": "https://example.com/#business",
  "name": "[Client business name]",
  "telephone": "+1-555-010-1234",
  "priceRange": "$$",
  "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "streetAddress": "[Street]", "addressLocality": "[City]", "addressRegion": "[State]", "postalCode": "[ZIP]" },
  "geo": { "@type": "GeoCoordinates", "latitude": 0, "longitude": 0 },
  "areaServed": ["[City]", "[Neighboring city]"],
  "openingHoursSpecification": [
    { "@type": "OpeningHoursSpecification", "dayOfWeek": ["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri"], "opens": "08:00", "closes": "18:00" }
  ],
  "aggregateRating": { "@type": "AggregateRating", "ratingValue": "4.8", "reviewCount": "126" }
}
```

Service node: `{ "@type": "Service", "serviceType": "[Service name]", "provider": { "@id": ".../#business" }, "areaServed": ["[City]"], "offers": { "@type": "Offer", "priceCurrency": "USD", "price": "[client-supplied]" } }`

## Content slots
- Legal name, address, phone, hours with holiday overrides — [Client-supplied; must match the footer and Google Business Profile exactly].
- Service list matching the visible services grid — [Client-supplied].
- FAQ pairs matching the visible FAQ — [Client-supplied].
- Review rating and count — pulled live from the same source rendered on the page, never a static placeholder.

## Interaction & motion
Not applicable — no interactive or animated surface.

## Accessibility
Not applicable to the schema itself. Binding rule: mark up only content actually visible and readable on the page. Never mark up a hidden FAQ answer or a rating the visitor cannot also see.

## Performance
Inline the JSON-LD in the initial server-rendered HTML — never client-side or fetched separately. Scope each block to its page, not one graph spanning the site. Compute values from data already fetched for the visible content.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: `HVACBusiness`; `areaServed` as a radius or city list matching dispatch range.
- Salon/spa: `HairSalon`/`BeautySalon`; Service nodes map to menu items, duration as an added property.
- Fitness studio: `ExerciseGym`/`SportsActivityLocation`; add `Course`/`Event` only if a schedule is visible.
- Cleaning service: `HomeAndConstructionBusiness`; `areaServed` often a radius, not named cities.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Every LocalBusiness node validates in a structured-data testing tool with no errors.
- [ ] Address, phone and hours match the footer and Google Business Profile character-for-character.
- [ ] Multi-location sites emit one distinct node per location, each with a unique `@id`.
- [ ] AggregateRating values are generated from the same source as the visible rating, never hardcoded.
- [ ] FAQPage schema exists only on pages with a matching, visible FAQ.
- [ ] No schema property describes content absent from the rendered page.
- [ ] All JSON-LD is present in server-rendered initial HTML, not injected client-side.

title: Map, Contact & Booking Block
our_text:
# Map, Contact & Booking Block

The bottom-of-page conversion block for an S1 local-business homepage. This is the
visitor's last chance to act before leaving the page, so it carries every remaining
path to contact: map, address with directions, hours (including holiday overrides),
phone, a short contact form, and the booking entry point. Done means all six pieces
work independently, none of them blocks first paint, and no tracking fires before
consent.

## Structure
1. Section heading — orients the block as the closing action, e.g. "Get in touch"
2. Map — static placeholder until interaction, then a real embed
3. Address — full postal address plus a directions link
4. Hours — regular hours per day, with holiday overrides shown separately
5. Phone — visible, tap-to-call
6. Contact form — name, phone, email, message
7. Booking entry point — button or link into the booking flow

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<640px): single column, static map image first, form full width below it.
Tablet (640–1024px): two columns — map and address/hours left, form and booking
button right. Desktop (>1024px): same two-column grid, map enlarged, block
constrained to the page's max content width. Nothing reflows below two columns;
above it, columns only widen.

## Typography
Section heading at display-small scale. Labels (form fields, hours days) at the
label scale. Body text (address, hours values, form helper text) at base scale,
modular ratio ~1.25, line length 60–75ch for any paragraph content.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface`, `--ink`, `--accent`, `--muted`, `--border`. Body text meets 4.5:1
against `--surface`; form field borders, the map placeholder border, and button
boundaries meet 3:1.

## Components
- **Map**: static placeholder (default) → consent/loading → error/blocked → loaded.
- **Directions link**: default, hover, focus-visible, active.
- **Hours list**: default row; holiday-override row is visually distinct (not by
  colour alone — add a label like "Closed" or a date range).
- **Contact form**: default, per-field focus-visible, inline + summary error,
  submitting, success, disabled-submit while invalid.
- **Booking button**: default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled (while the
  booking adapter loads).

## Content slots
Address (street, city, state, ZIP) — single source of truth, reused by the schema
pack. Hours — regular schedule plus `[Client to supply holiday schedule]`. Phone
number — must match header and footer exactly. Map location — address or lat/long
for geocoding. Form recipient — client or agency CRM endpoint. Any unfilled slot
shows obviously-fake placeholder text, e.g. `[Business Name]`, `[Service Area]`.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: micro, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. The map iframe loads only
after a user click or consent action — never automatically. Form focus and error
states use a simple CSS transition. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all
transitions; state changes become instant.

## Accessibility
Keyboard path: heading → map trigger button → directions link → hours (static
text) → phone (tel: link, accessible name states the full number) → form fields
in visual order with visible labels → error summary linked to fields via
`aria-describedby` → booking button. All targets ≥44×44px. Visible focus ring on
every interactive element at 3:1 contrast. The map iframe, once loaded, has a
`title` attribute and is not a keyboard trap.

## Performance
This block sits below the fold, so it must not affect the page's LCP. The map
embed loads only on interaction/consent; its pre-consent placeholder is a static
image with explicit width and height. No map or analytics script fires before
consent is given. Form validation JS is deferred, never render-blocking.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: map emphasizes service-area radius; show an emergency phone distinct from
  the office line.
- Salon/spa: booking button is primary, form is secondary; hours note
  by-appointment variations.
- Fitness studio: map callout notes parking/entrance; hours link out to the class
  schedule.
- Cleaning service: form doubles as a quote request, adding property type and size
  fields.

## Acceptance checks
1. Map issues no network request until the user interacts or consents.
2. Static map placeholder has explicit width/height; no layout shift on swap.
3. Phone number is a `tel:` link with an accessible name stating the full number.
4. Every form field has a visible, programmatically associated label.
5. Form errors are linked to their field via `aria-describedby` and summarized at
   the top.
6. Holiday hours are distinguishable from regular hours by more than colour.
7. Directions link opens to the client's exact supplied address.
8. Every interactive element shows a focus ring meeting 3:1 contrast.
9. No third-party tracking script fires before consent.
10. Booking entry point is reachable by keyboard in one tab stop from the form.

title: Local Trust Proof Strip
our_text:
# Local Trust Proof Strip

A narrow band directly under the hero on the S1 skeleton. Its only job is
credibility: licence status, insurance, years in business, certifications,
and aggregate review rating, in one honest glance. This is the highest-trust
element on the page — done looks like every figure being true, sourced, and
never inflated by design.

## Structure

1. Full-width band, directly below the hero, above the services grid.
2. 3–5 proof items in a row: licence/insurance status, years in business,
   certifications/affiliations, aggregate review rating (with count), and an
   optional local badge (e.g. "Locally owned").
3. Each item pairs a short label with a value — no paragraph copy.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile (`<640px`): horizontal scroll-snap if items exceed viewport width,
with a visible affordance (partial next item showing), not hidden overflow.
Tablet and desktop (`≥640px`): items wrap into a static, evenly spaced row.
Item order stays fixed across breakpoints.

## Typography

Label role for the caption (e.g. "Licensed & insured"), 13–14px, medium
weight, `--muted`. Value role for the figure (e.g. "15+ years"), body role
16–18px, `--ink`, bold enough to scan quickly. No display-scale text here —
this is a supporting strip, not a second hero.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` for the band background (may alias the page surface, still
≥4.5:1 against `--ink`). `--ink` for values, `--muted` for labels (≥4.5:1
against `--surface`). `--border` for dividers between items, ≥3:1. `--accent`
reserved for the rating value only, never for decoration.

## Components

**Proof item**: optional decorative icon (`aria-hidden`) + label + value, as
a non-interactive group unless the item links out (e.g. rating links to
`/reviews`). States: default; if linked, hover and focus-visible only. Static
figures (licence, years) have no loading state — they are build-time content.
A live rating figure has a loading state (skeleton at final size) and a
static fallback if the source is unavailable, never a blank gap.

## Content slots

Licence/insurance status, years in business, certification/affiliation
names, aggregate rating and review count, optional local-ownership badge.
Every value is client-supplied: `[License # — client to supply]`, `[XX years
in business]`, `[Certification name]`, `[4.X★ — XXX reviews]`. A slot with no
client figure is omitted entirely, never filled with an invented value.

## Interaction & motion

None by default beyond the shared ≤150ms hover/focus feedback on linked
items (opacity/transform only). No animated counters, no marquee/ticker, no
entrance animation on scroll into view. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is a
no-op here since hover/focus is the only motion and already complies.

## Accessibility

Each item's label and value are programmatically associated, not conveyed by
icon colour alone. Decorative icons are `aria-hidden="true"`; text carries
the meaning. Linked items meet the 44×44px touch-target floor and show a
focus indicator ≥3:1. Text contrast: 4.5:1 for values/labels, 3:1 for
dividers. The band is fully keyboard-reachable via standard tab order, not
scroll-only, even under mobile scroll-snap.

## Performance

Reserve the band's height at build time so it never pushes the services grid
after load. If the rating figure is fetched from a third party, it renders
behind a same-size skeleton and never blocks the strip's static items from
painting immediately.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: leads with 24-hour/emergency availability and brand certifications
  ahead of years in business.
- Salon/spa: certifications slot becomes stylist licensing or product-line
  partnerships; rating often leads.
- Fitness: replaces licence/insurance with membership count or trainer
  certifications, where real figures exist.
- Cleaning: bonding and insurance status is the lead item, non-negotiable for
  this vertical.
- Item count and order change per vertical; the band's structure, states,
  and no-motion rule hold everywhere.

## Acceptance checks

1. Band renders directly between the hero and the services grid, full width.
2. Every item pairs a label and a value with no orphaned figures.
3. No item displays a fabricated or unsourced statistic.
4. Any item without a client-supplied figure is omitted, not invented.
5. A linked rating item is keyboard-reachable and shows visible focus.
6. Text contrast meets 4.5:1 for values/labels, 3:1 for dividers.
7. No animation beyond ≤150ms hover/focus on linked items.
8. Band height is reserved at build time; no shift when a live rating loads.
9. Mobile overflow uses visible scroll-snap, not hidden or clipped content.

title: Local Reviews Section
our_text:
# Local Reviews Section

Section prompt for the third-party review display on an S1 homepage, after the about/trust block and before map/contact/booking. This is proof pulled from outside the business, so its value depends on being real and current. Done means the rating and reviews render correctly when the source is fast, degrade honestly when it is slow, and never show fabricated content when it fails.

## Structure

1. Aggregate summary — star rating, review count, platform name/logo.
2. Review list — 3–6 reviews: reviewer name, rating, excerpt, date.
3. Outbound link — "See all reviews on [platform]" linking to the source page.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile (<640px): single column, reviews stacked as cards, aggregate summary full-width above.
Tablet (640–1023px): two-column grid or a horizontally scrollable row (state which).
Desktop (≥1024px): three-column review grid, aggregate summary left-aligned or centered above.
Internal card/summary structure does not change across breakpoints — only the column count.

## Typography

Aggregate rating number: role "display-sm", the section's largest element. Review count/platform name: role "label", `--muted`. Reviewer name: role "label-lg", medium weight. Excerpt: role "body", 1rem, 45–65 character lines, 2–4 lines — let cards vary in height, no text clamping. Date: role "label", small, `--muted`.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` — card/section background. `--ink` — excerpt/reviewer name, 4.5:1. `--muted` — date, count, platform name, 4.5:1. `--accent` — star fill and outbound link, 3:1; stars pair with a visible numeric rating, never color-only. `--border` — card outline, 3:1.

## Components

**AggregateSummary** — rating number, star icons (decorative, paired with visible numeric text), review count, platform wordmark/link.
- Default: fully rendered. Loading: skeleton matching final dimensions, region `aria-busy="true"`.
- Error/blocked (widget failed, tracker-blocked, timed out): falls back to a static message — "Reviews are provided by [platform]. View them directly at [outbound link]." No number shows if it cannot be verified live; never an estimated figure.
- Empty (zero reviews): section hides itself or shows "No reviews yet — be the first," never a fabricated placeholder.

**ReviewCard** — reviewer name, star rating, excerpt, date. Default; hover/focus-visible only if the whole card links out. No fabricated content is ever hardcoded — `[Review data — pulled from platform integration]` stands in during build, never an invented reviewer or quote.

## Content slots

- `platform`: the third-party source (Google, Yelp, an industry site), client-supplied; sets the outbound link.
- `aggregateRating` / `reviewCount`: pulled live, never hand-entered or estimated.
- `reviews[]`: pulled live; each `{ author, rating, excerpt, date }`. No manually authored content ships.
- `outboundLink`: URL to the business's profile on the source platform.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: micro. Horizontal card scroll, if used, is native and manual — no carousel autoplay. Hover/focus transitions ≤150ms, color/underline only. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables scroll-snap easing in favor of instant native scroll, not merely slowing it.

## Accessibility

- Aggregate rating is announced as text ("4.8 out of 5 stars, 127 reviews"), not star icons alone.
- Loading state sets `aria-busy="true"`; error/empty states show real, readable text, never an empty container.
- A horizontally scrolling card row is keyboard-operable with a visible focus indicator.
- Outbound link has a descriptive accessible name (e.g. "See all 127 reviews on Google"), not bare "click here."
- Section heading is a sibling of the about/trust section's heading.

## Performance

Never the LCP element by design — the review widget or its fetch must not block first paint or the hero's LCP. Load data client-side after initial render, or server-render with a short revalidation window; never let a slow endpoint delay the rest of the page. Widget scripts load deferred/async, off the critical path. Skeleton state reserves the loaded state's exact dimensions.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: excerpts favor emergency-response/reliability language when present — never rewrite review text.
- Salon/spa: reviews may reference a specific stylist by name if present in source data.
- Fitness: aggregate rating may note typical response time only if verifiably true.
- Cleaning: bonding/insurance trust lives in the about section; this stays purely review content.

## Acceptance checks

1. Aggregate rating always pairs with visible numeric text, never star icons alone.
2. Loading state reserves final layout dimensions — no shift when data arrives.
3. A blocked or failed widget shows an honest fallback message and outbound link, never a stale or fabricated number.
4. The zero-review state never renders a placeholder review that looks real.
5. No review content in the shipped build is hand-authored or invented.
6. The outbound link has a descriptive accessible name and meets the 44×44px target.
7. No autoplay or auto-rotating carousel is present.

title: Salon & Spa Site
our_text:
# Salon & Spa Site

Complete homepage for a hair salon or day spa: 1–9 stylists or therapists, service
menu with pricing, and booking as the primary action. The job is to move a visitor
from "what do they offer and what does it cost" to a confirmed appointment with a
named person. Done means the price list is readable, every stylist has a face
and name attached to booking, and real work shows without a gallery that fights
the phone.

## Structure

1. Header — logo, phone, nav, "Book now" at every scroll position.
2. Hero — offer and tone in copy, one photo, CTA books.
3. Service menu with pricing — grouped by category, each line priced or ranged.
4. Stylist/therapist profiles — photo, name, specialty, "Book with [name]".
5. Gallery — real work, grid-based, no autoplay carousel.
6. Proof strip — years in business, certifications, rating, product lines.
7. About/trust — origin story, philosophy, hygiene note if wanted.
8. Reviews.
9. Location, hours, booking block.
10. Footer.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile 360–767px: single column, menu as stacked accordions, stylist cards stack, gallery 2 columns. Tablet 768–1023px: menu two-column, gallery 3 columns. Desktop 1024px+: stylists 3–4 across, gallery 4 columns, menu stays two-column. Booking button stays reachable in the header at every breakpoint.

## Typography

Roles: display, body, label, and a `price` role in a tabular-figure variant so numbers align down the menu. Modular scale ~1.2, tighter than a trade site, since price density matters more than headline size. Line length 50–75ch for prose; price rows exempt.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--ink` (4.5:1), `--accent` (booking CTA, active states, 3:1 against surface), `--muted` for price qualifiers, `--border` for menu-row dividers. No token implies a palette — client identity, not a house look.

## Components

**Header/Nav** — default, scrolled, focus-visible; booking button always links out, never disabled. **ServiceMenuAccordion** — collapsed/expanded, keyboard-operable, server-rendered with JS off. **StylistCard** — default, hover, focus-visible, skeleton, "unavailable" fallback. **Gallery** — focus-visible grid item; enlarging opens a full-size view, not a scripted lightbox. **ProofStrip** — static. **ReviewsSection** — loading, populated, empty, blocked. **BookingBlock** — default, and "fully booked" capturing a waitlist contact.

## Content slots

Business name, phone, hours, service menu `[Service — description — price/range]`, stylist name/photo/specialty/years `[Bio — 1–2 sentences]`, gallery images with alt text describing the result, certifications or product-line names, testimonials `[Client testimonial — 2 sentences]`, booking link or embed.

## Interaction & motion

Micro budget: hover/focus feedback only, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. The gallery's full-size view is a same-page expansion or linked image, not a carousel — this trade's usual default, rejected here. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the accordion transition entirely. No parallax, WebGL, or autoplay video.

## Accessibility

Service menu accordions are real disclosure widgets: `button` triggers, `aria-expanded`, keyboard-reachable with visible focus. "Book with [name]" links are unambiguous, never a bare "Book". Gallery images carry descriptive alt text, not filenames. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Contrast 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text/UI boundaries.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading or photo — name whichever the build produces. Gallery images lazy-load with explicit width/height; the hero image gets `fetchpriority="high"`. Webfonts use `font-display: swap` with matched fallback metrics — a shifting price list is a trust problem. Booking widgets load deferred, never blocking first paint.

## Vertical adaptation

- Stylist/therapist profiles are first-class, with individual booking actions — clients book a person, deeper than any other S1 vertical.
- The service menu with pricing replaces the generic services grid as core content; price density matters more than card imagery.
- The gallery is real-work photography, built without a heavy lightbox — this trade defaults to carousels harder than any other, so the rejection is stated.
- Proof strip includes product lines carried, specific to salons/spas.
- Booking has a "fully booked" state capturing a waitlist contact, since demand is schedule-bound in a way emergency trades are not.

## Acceptance checks

- Every stylist card has a booking link naming that person.
- Service menu is a real accordion: keyboard-operable, `aria-expanded` correct, content present with JS off.
- Gallery has no autoplaying carousel and no third-party lightbox.
- Prices align in a tabular-figure column at desktop.
- Booking button is reachable at every scroll position, mobile and desktop.
- Gallery images carry descriptive, non-generic alt text.
- Contrast of `--accent` against `--surface` is 3:1+ on the booking CTA.
- Reviews falls back to a static rating when the widget is blocked.

title: Service Detail Page Template
our_text:
# Service Detail Page Template

Template for `/service/{slug}` on an S1 local-business site. One service explained
in enough depth to satisfy local search intent and to move a reader from "what is
this" to "call or book." Done means the page stands alone for someone landing from
search, links back to the services grid, and ends in a booking CTA.

## Structure
1. Breadcrumb — Home > Services > [Service]
2. Header (shared) — phone and service area
3. Hero — service name (H1), one-line summary, primary CTA
4. What it covers — scope description
5. Pricing — cost or how pricing works
6. Timeline — how long the service takes
7. Preparation — what the customer needs to do or provide
8. FAQ
9. Related services — links back to the services grid
10. Booking/contact CTA band
11. Footer (shared)

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<640px): single column; FAQ renders as an accordion; primary CTA is
reinforced by the sticky call bar. Tablet (640–1024px): content constrained to
~680px, still single column, a CTA sidebar appears. Desktop (>1024px): two
columns — content ~65% left, a sticky sidebar (price, CTA, prep checklist) right,
which unsticks after the FAQ section ends.

## Typography
H1 at display scale. Section headings at H2, modular scale ~1.25. Body copy at
base scale, 60–75ch line length. FAQ questions at H3 or label weight, answers at
base scale.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface`, `--ink`, `--accent`, `--muted`, `--border`. Body text 4.5:1 against
`--surface`; price emphasis text and card borders 3:1.

## Components
- **Breadcrumb**: default, hover, focus-visible.
- **Sidebar CTA card**: default, sticky, focus-visible button, disabled if booking
  is unavailable (falls back to phone/contact).
- **Pricing block**: default (range or "starting at"), empty (no price supplied —
  shows "Call for a quote").
- **FAQ accordion**: collapsed/expanded, focus-visible, keyboard-operable
  (Enter/Space toggles).
- **Related services list**: default, hover, focus-visible link cards.

## Content slots
Service name, one-line summary, full description (150–300 words), price or
pricing model `[Client to confirm pricing display]`, typical duration, a bulleted
preparation checklist, 3–6 FAQ pairs, 2–4 related-service links. Any unfilled slot
uses obviously-fake placeholder copy, e.g. `[Service description — 2–3
paragraphs]`.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: micro, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, limited to the FAQ
expand/collapse and hover/focus feedback. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
removes the accordion animation — content snaps open or closed instantly.

## Accessibility
Keyboard path: breadcrumb → H1 → body content → FAQ accordion (each item
independently focusable and operable) → related-service links → sidebar CTA.
Heading levels are strictly nested, never skipped. FAQ uses a native disclosure
pattern or `aria-expanded` on its trigger. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Focus-visible
on every interactive element at 3:1 contrast.

## Performance
LCP element is the H1 or hero summary text; this template needs no hero image. If
a photo is used, it carries explicit width/height and `loading="lazy"` unless
above the fold, where it uses `fetchpriority="high"` instead. No render-blocking
third-party embeds above the fold. Webfonts load with `font-display: swap` and a
metric-matched fallback to prevent layout shift.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: preparation section covers access requirements (attic, breaker box);
  pricing is framed as diagnostic-fee-then-quote.
- Salon/spa: pricing renders as a menu-style list of service variants; prep
  covers arrival time and contraindications.
- Fitness studio: pricing is replaced by a class/membership tie-in; prep covers
  what to bring.
- Cleaning service: pricing is framed by frequency and property size, and links
  to the instant-quote estimator instead of a static figure.

## Acceptance checks
1. Page has exactly one H1; heading levels never skip.
2. Breadcrumb links back to the services grid with a correct href.
3. FAQ items are keyboard-operable and expose `aria-expanded` state.
4. Pricing block renders a "call for quote" fallback when no price is supplied.
5. Sidebar CTA stays reachable and visible at all three breakpoints.
6. Every content slot without client copy shows clearly-fake placeholder text.
7. No image is missing explicit width/height attributes.
8. Related-services links point to real service slugs, never the current page.
9. A booking/contact CTA appears in both the sidebar and the closing CTA band.

title: Local Services Grid
our_text:
# Local Services Grid

Section prompt for the offerings grid on an S1 local-business homepage, and the block other S1 pages link back to. Sits between the trust proof strip and the about/trust section. Done means a visitor scanning for two seconds understands what the business does, picks a service, and reaches its detail page without confusion — on a phone, with a keyboard, or with a screen reader.

## Structure

1. Section heading — names the block ("What we do" or client equivalent) with an optional sub-line.
2. Card grid — four to six service cards, one per offering.
3. Each card: title, one-line audience statement, optional price signal, whole card as one link.

## Layout & responsive

Mobile (<640px): single column, cards stacked, full-width.
Tablet (640–1023px): two-column grid.
Desktop (≥1024px): three-column grid; four- and five-card sets wrap unevenly rather than forcing an empty slot.
Grid uses CSS Grid with `align-items: stretch` so every card matches its tallest row sibling — stretch, not fixed heights, so uneven copy never clips or overflows. Card layout is flex column with the price/CTA line pushed to the bottom via `margin-top: auto`.

## Typography

Card title: role "label-lg", one step above body (e.g. 1.125rem), medium weight.
Audience line and description: role "body", 1rem, 2–3 lines. Write to fit — no ellipsis truncation, which strands screen-reader users mid-sentence.
Price signal (if present): role "label", distinguished by weight, not color alone.
Line length inside a card: 45–65 characters.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (card background), `--surface-raised` if on a tinted section — 3:1 boundary contrast against `--surface`.
`--ink` (title, body) — 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
`--muted` (audience line, price label) — 4.5:1 against `--surface`, never color-only for meaning.
`--accent` (focus ring, hover border) — 3:1 against `--surface`.
`--border` (card outline) — 3:1 against `--surface`.

## Components

**ServiceCard** — props: `title`, `audience`, `description`, `priceSignal?`, `href`.
- Default: bordered card, `--border` outline, no shadow required.
- Hover (pointer only): border shifts to `--accent`, ≤150ms.
- Focus-visible: visible outline on the whole card link, ≥2px, `--accent`, never suppressed.
- Active: brief border/background shift, ≤150ms.
- No loading, disabled, or empty states apply — static, client-authored content. Fewer than four services renders that many cards, no placeholder filler.

## Content slots

- `title`: 2–4 words, client-supplied.
- `audience`: one sentence, who this is for, ≤80 characters.
- `description`: one sentence, what it covers, ≤120 characters.
- `priceSignal`: optional, e.g. "From $X" — omit rather than inventing one; never a placeholder number.
- `href`: link to `/service/{slug}`.
Placeholder copy during build must read as obviously fake, e.g. `[Service name — client to supply]`.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: micro. Hover/focus feedback only, border/background transitions ≤150ms, transform limited to a 2px lift if used. No stagger-in, no scroll-triggered reveal. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the hover/focus transition entirely rather than shortening it.

## Accessibility

- Each card is a single `<a>` wrapping the whole card — one tab stop per card.
- Tab order follows visual reading order.
- Touch target is the full card, always ≥44×44px.
- Card title is the link's accessible name; audience, description and price are supplementary text inside it.
- Section heading sits one level below the page's H1.

## Performance

Not the typical LCP element (the hero usually is) — confirm per page. No images required by default; client-supplied icons use inline SVG or sized raster with explicit `width`/`height` and `loading="lazy"`. No layout shift from font loading.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: titles lean toward emergency/seasonal naming ("24-hour repair") over generic categories.
- Salon/spa: price signal becomes near-mandatory; pair with "book" instead of "contact" where scheduling is live.
- Fitness: cards may represent class types or membership tiers; audience line carries fitness level, not just persona.
- Cleaning: cards separate by frequency (one-time vs. recurring); price signal is often "instant quote" rather than a number.

## Acceptance checks

1. Grid renders 4–6 cards without an empty placeholder slot at any breakpoint.
2. Every card is reachable and activatable via keyboard alone, in visual order.
3. No card's clickable area is smaller than the full card boundary.
4. Uneven copy in one card does not change sibling card height in its row.
5. Focus indicator is visible on every card at ≥2px against `--surface`.
6. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes hover/focus transitions rather than shortening them.
7. No price signal appears unless client-supplied.
8. All text meets its stated contrast ratio against `--surface`.

title: Local Service Homepage Skeleton
our_text:
# Local Service Homepage Skeleton

The reference homepage for the S1 kit: a 1–9 employee local business — trades,
salon, fitness studio, cleaning company, small clinic. The job is credibility
and lead capture, not e-commerce. Done looks like a visitor finding the phone
number, service area, and one proof point in a single scroll, then calling or
booking. Every other S1 prompt slots into the region order defined here — its
names and the header/footer contract are fixed points others depend on.
Routes: `/`, `/services`, `/service/{slug}`, `/about`, `/reviews`, `/booking`,
`/contact`, `/thank-you`.

## Structure

1. **Header** — name/logo, nav, tap-to-call phone, service-area badge.
2. **Hero** — trade, area, phone, booking CTA above the fold. (`zs-s1-hero`)
3. **Proof strip** — licence, insurance, years, rating. (`zs-s1-proof-strip`)
4. **Services grid** — 4–6 cards to `/service/{slug}`. (`zs-s1-services-grid`)
5. **About & trust** — owner/team photo, story, credentials.
   (`zs-s1-about-trust`)
6. **Reviews** — aggregate rating and reviews. (`zs-s1-reviews`)
7. **Map, contact & booking** — closing block. (`zs-s1-map-contact-booking`)
8. **Footer** — NAP, hours, service area, licences, legal. (`zs-s1-footer`)

LocalBusiness JSON-LD is emitted site-wide, not a visible region.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Content
column max-width 1280px, centred, 16/24/32px gutters. Header nav collapses to
a hamburger below tablet; logo and phone never collapse. Services grid:
1/2/3 columns across the breakpoints. Proof strip scrolls horizontally on
mobile if items overflow, wraps static from tablet up. Footer: single column
mobile, 3–4 columns desktop. Nothing reflows on scroll.

## Typography

Roles: display (headline), heading (section titles), body, label (nav,
buttons, fields). Modular scale, 1.25 ratio, 16px base: label 14px, body
16px, heading 24–32px, display 36–48px. Body line length 60–75ch. Headings
are real elements in document order, never used for weight alone.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (bg, ≥4.5:1 vs `--ink`), `--ink` (primary text), `--accent`
(CTAs/links, ≥3:1 vs `--surface`), `--muted` (secondary text, ≥4.5:1),
`--border` (dividers, ≥3:1), `--focus-ring` (≥3:1). No hex values or brand
names — the client's palette maps onto these tokens.

## Components

**Header**: logo/name, nav list, `tel:` phone link, service-area badge, mobile
menu toggle. States: default, hover, focus-visible, active, menu-open.
**Footer**: NAP block matching schema, hours, service-area list, licence
numbers, social/legal links. States: default, hover, focus-visible. A
persistent mobile sticky call bar overlays every route — full spec in
`zs-s1-sticky-call-bar`.

## Content slots

Business name, logo, phone number, service-area list, nav labels, hours (with
holiday overrides), licence numbers, social/legal URLs — each ships as an
obvious placeholder (`[Business name]`), never a plausible fabricated value.

## Interaction & motion

Avoid by default. Hover/focus-visible only, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only —
no scroll choreography, parallax, WebGL, or autoplay video anywhere in the
skeleton or its children. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` drops all
durations to 0ms.

## Accessibility

Skip-to-content link as the first focusable element. Landmarks: `header`,
`nav`, `main`, `footer`. One `h1` per page, in the hero; strictly descending
heading order. Visible focus indicator ≥3:1 on every interactive element.
Touch targets ≥44×44px. Contrast 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text/UI. Keyboard
path: skip link → nav → phone link → hero CTAs → sections in DOM order →
footer, no trap.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero headline or photograph — defined in `zs-s1-hero`; this
skeleton reserves its exact box so nothing shifts. Header logo as SVG or sized
WebP; images ship explicit width/height. Webfonts use `font-display: swap`
with a matched fallback. Map, review widget, and booking scheduler load
below the fold, deferred or on interaction — none render-blocking.

## Vertical adaptation

- HVAC: proof strip leads with emergency/24-hour availability.
- Salon/spa: services grid becomes a priced menu; about foregrounds stylists.
- Fitness: hero CTA is a free-trial offer ahead of "book."
- Cleaning: instant-quote entry sits under the hero.
- All verticals keep the eight-region order fixed; only emphasis shifts.

## Acceptance checks

1. All eight regions render in order, DOM matching visual order.
2. Header phone is a real `tel:` link, visible without scrolling.
3. Exactly one `h1` exists, inside the hero.
4. Every interactive element shows a visible focus indicator on keyboard nav.
5. Footer NAP data matches the LocalBusiness schema exactly.
6. No motion exceeds 150ms or animates outside opacity/transform, and
   `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes it entirely.
7. No content slot renders a fabricated detail or statistic.
8. Map, review, and booking embeds do not block first paint.

title: Sticky Call & Contact Bar
our_text:
# Sticky Call & Contact Bar

A persistent mobile bar for an S1 local-business site that keeps call, directions,
and book one tap away on every page. Done means it never covers content or a form
field, respects the on-screen keyboard, can be dismissed, never traps focus, and
behaves differently — deliberately — on desktop.

## Structure
1. Call action — tap-to-call, primary
2. Directions action — opens the map/directions target
3. Book action — links to the booking entry point
4. Dismiss control — closes the bar for the session

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<768px): fixed to the viewport bottom, full width, three icon-plus-label
actions in a row, dismiss control in the corner. The bar stays put — no
hide-on-scroll — since appearing and disappearing while scrolling is more
disorienting than a persistent bar. Tablet/desktop (≥768px): this component does
not render at all; the same three actions live in the persistent header instead.

## Typography
Icon-plus-label pairs at the label-scale token. No heading role — this is a
persistent control, not page content.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface`, `--ink`, `--accent`, `--border`. Bar background uses `--surface`
with a 3:1 boundary against the page behind it; each icon/label pair meets 4.5:1
against `--surface`.

## Components
- **Bar container**: visible (default) → dismissed (hidden for the session, no
  re-trigger control). Dismissal state persists in session storage, not a
  permanent cookie.
- **Call / Directions / Book buttons**: default, focus-visible, active, and
  disabled (Book falls back to Call/Contact if the booking adapter fails to
  load).
- **Dismiss control**: default, focus-visible, active.

## Content slots
Phone number, directions target, and booking link are all reused from the shared
header/footer and the map/contact block — this component introduces no new copy
of its own.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: micro, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, applied solely to the
dismiss transition. There is no entrance animation — the bar is present on load,
not animated in. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the dismiss transition
entirely; the bar disappears instantly.

## Accessibility
The bar is a landmark region (e.g. `role="region" aria-label="Quick contact"`)
outside the main content flow, so screen-reader users can skip it. It must never
overlap a focusable element — reserve equivalent bottom padding on the page body.
When a form field's on-screen keyboard would cover the bar, the bar must not
intercept or trap focus; verify this on a real device, not just a resized
viewport. Touch targets ≥44×44px with ≥8px spacing between them. The dismiss
control has an accessible name ("Close quick contact bar") and returns focus to
whatever previously held it.

## Performance
This component adds no content to LCP and must not delay the page's actual LCP
element. It renders from data already loaded on the page — phone, directions, and
booking values — with no separate client-side fetch.

## Vertical adaptation
- HVAC: Call is the default primary action, reflecting emergency-service urgency.
- Salon/spa: Book is primary, Call secondary.
- Fitness studio: Book (free trial) is primary; Directions may be replaced by
  "Schedule" where class booking dominates.
- Cleaning service: Call plus a quote-request shortcut replace Directions, since
  most inquiries arrive by phone or form, not walk-in.

## Acceptance checks
1. Bar renders only below the 768px breakpoint; above it, its actions exist only
   in the header.
