2. Bar never overlaps a focusable element — the page reserves bottom padding
   equal to the bar's height.
3. Dismissing the bar does not trap focus; focus returns to the previously
   focused element.
4. Call action is a `tel:` link with an accessible name stating the full number.
5. All three actions and the dismiss control meet the 44×44px touch target
   minimum.
6. Bar does not cover or intercept form fields when the on-screen keyboard is
   open.
7. No entrance animation runs on load; only the dismiss transition animates, and
   only outside `prefers-reduced-motion`.
8. Bar is marked as a landmark region with an accessible name distinct from main
   content.

title: Consultation Booking Block
our_text:
# Consultation Booking Block

The block where a prospective client books time with a professional firm — consultation type, duration, availability and what to bring — plus a secure channel for sensitive detail that should never travel by plain email. Done = a visitor can book a real slot, or find another path, without ever being told to email sensitive information in the clear.

## Structure
1. Consultation type selector — offerings (e.g. free 15-minute screen, paid consultation), each with duration and price if applicable.
2. Availability calendar — open slots for the selected type, filtered by provider or location where relevant.
3. Preparation notice — what the client should have ready: documents, questions, ID.
4. Secure contact alternative — a link to a secure channel for sensitive detail, positioned as the non-email path.
5. Confirmation state — booking summary, calendar-add action, reminder expectation.
6. No-availability fallback — waitlist or callback request when no slots are open.

## Layout & responsive
Mobile (<640px): stacked — type selector, calendar as a scrollable day list, preparation notice. Tablet (640–1024px): calendar shows a 3-day view. Desktop (>1024px): calendar shows a week grid, type selector as a sidebar. Preparation notice and the secure-contact link stay full-width below the calendar at every size — never pushed below the fold on mobile.

## Typography
Type name: label role, 15–16px, weight 600. Duration/price: body role, 14px, `--muted`. Calendar labels: label role, 14px, tabular figures so columns align. Section headings ("Prepare for your consultation"): display-small, one step above body.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface` (4.5:1 against `--ink`), `--ink` (primary text), `--accent` (selected type/slot, primary CTA, 3:1), `--border` (calendar and card borders, 3:1), `--muted` (duration/price, 4.5:1). Selected states use `--accent` plus a visible border change, never colour alone.

## Components
- Type card: name, duration, price or "no charge". States: default, hover, focus-visible, selected, disabled (fully booked).
- Time-slot grid: one button per slot. States: available, selected, unavailable (`aria-disabled`, not removed from the DOM), loading.
- Secure-contact link: labelled ("Send sensitive details securely"), routes to an encrypted form or client portal, never a mailto for anything beyond a name and general inquiry.
- Confirmation card: date/time, provider or type, "add to calendar", cancellation/reschedule link.
- Waitlist/callback form: name, contact, preferred window — shown only when the selected type has zero open slots.

## Content slots
Type names, durations and prices `[Client-supplied]`. Preparation checklist items `[Client-supplied]`. Secure-contact channel and provider `[Client-supplied, e.g. their client portal]`. Confirmation/reminder cadence `[Client-supplied, e.g. "reminder 24 hours before"]` — never assume a reminder channel the firm hasn't confirmed.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: micro. Selecting a type or slot updates state with a ≤150ms opacity/background change only. Calendar navigation swaps content instantly, no slide animation. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes even that ≤150ms change — it becomes instant.

## Accessibility
Type cards and time slots are real buttons, keyboard-operable, 44×44px minimum. Selected state uses `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected`, not colour alone. The calendar grid is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys move between days/times) with a focus ring meeting 3:1 contrast. Unavailable slots carry `aria-disabled="true"` with a text reason ("Fully booked"), not silent removal. Loading state announces via `aria-live="polite"` ("Loading available times"). Waitlist/callback fields follow the same labelled-control and error-association rules as the intake form.

## Performance
LCP element is the type selector — first meaningful content, no image. Calendar data loads client-side after initial paint; type selector and preparation notice render server-side and are usable before availability resolves. Any third-party scheduling embed loads behind a native placeholder sized to prevent layout shift, never blocking first paint.

## Vertical adaptation
- Law: types split by practice area; add a conflict-check disclaimer near the selector, not only at intake.
- Financial advisory: show fee basis per type (flat, hourly, no-cost) — fee transparency is part of the trust signal.
- Medical/dental: calendar carries an insurance/self-pay flag per slot; secure-contact link routes to a patient-portal message, never a general form.
- Consulting: longer durations (30–60 minute discovery calls); preparation notice covers "goals and current state" rather than documents.

## Acceptance checks
1. Every type card and time slot is a real, keyboard-operable button at least 44×44px.
2. Selected state is exposed via `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected`, not colour alone.
3. Unavailable slots carry `aria-disabled` and a text reason, not silent removal.
4. Calendar loading state announces via `aria-live`.
5. Secure-contact link never resolves to a plain mailto for sensitive detail.
6. Waitlist form appears only when the selected type has no open slots.
7. Contrast meets 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 borders and focus rings.
8. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all state-change transitions.
9. Confirmation state shows a calendar-add action and a reschedule/cancel path.

title: Per-Vertical Compliance Checklist
our_text:
# Per-Vertical Compliance Checklist

A pre-launch checklist component for professional-services builds, covering advertising and disclaimer rules, privacy and data handling, accessibility conformance, cookie and tracking consent, and records retention, organized by vertical (legal, financial advisory, healthcare, consulting). This is build guidance for what the site must technically support so the firm can meet its obligations. It is not legal advice, and it does not replace review by the firm's own compliance counsel before launch. Done = every item is checkable pass/fail against the live site, with the reason it exists stated next to it.

## Structure
1. Checklist header — vertical selector, last-reviewed date.
2. Advertising & disclaimer section — claims, disclaimers, required language per vertical.
3. Privacy & data handling section — what's collected, where it's stored, retention.
4. Accessibility conformance section — WCAG 2.2 AA spot checks tied to this build.
5. Cookie & tracking consent section — consent banner behaviour, third-party scripts.
6. Records section — what must be retained, for how long, and where.
7. Sign-off block — space for the firm's compliance reviewer to record approval, dated.

## Layout & responsive
Single column at all breakpoints, grouped by section with a visible heading. Mobile (<640px): each item stacks label above reason text. Desktop (>1024px): checkbox, label and reason sit on one row up to a 900px max width, so reason text stays readable. No multi-column reflow — a checklist read out of order defeats its purpose.

## Typography
Section headings: display-small. Item label: body role, 15–16px, weight 500. Reason text: body role, 14px, `--muted`, max 70 characters per line. Sign-off labels: label role, 14px.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface` (4.5:1 against `--ink`), `--ink` (item label text), `--muted` (reason text, 4.5:1), `--border` (dividers and checkbox outline, 3:1), `--accent` (checked state, focus ring, 3:1). Checked items get a visible strike or fill change, never a colour-only shift.

## Components
- Checklist item: checkbox, label, one-line reason. States: unchecked, checked, focus-visible. Check state persists per session (local storage).
- Vertical selector: toggle or select that shows/hides vertical-specific items within each section. States: default, selected, focus-visible.
- Sign-off block: reviewer name, date, free-text notes. No submit action required — this is a record, not a backend form.

## Content slots
Vertical-specific item text (exact bar-advertising disclaimer wording, exact financial-promotion disclosure text, exact HIPAA notice requirements) `[Firm's compliance counsel supplies exact wording — this checklist states what must exist, not the wording itself]`. Retention periods `[Firm/jurisdiction-specific — never default a number]`. Reviewer name and date `[Filled at review time]`.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: static — no motion. Checking an item updates instantly with no transition. This is a working document, not a marketing surface; animation would be noise.

## Accessibility
Every checkbox has a visible label bound via `for`/`id`. Checked state uses a native `<input type="checkbox">`, not a custom div, so it reports correctly to assistive tech without extra ARIA. Section headings follow a logical, sequential order so the checklist is navigable by heading in a screen reader. Reason text sits in reading order right after its item's label, never in a tooltip or hover-only disclosure. Focus-visible outlines on checkboxes and the vertical selector meet 3:1 contrast. Touch target (checkbox plus its label, as one hit area) meets 44×44px.

## Performance
No images, no client-side data fetching — static content plus local-storage checkbox state, hydrating a small client island only for that persistence; everything else server-renders. No LCP concern beyond standard text-paint budgets. No third-party scripts on this surface.

## Vertical adaptation
- Legal: bar-association advertising rules, case-result disclaimers, "no attorney-client relationship" language, jurisdictional licensing display.
- Financial advisory: fiduciary/registration disclosures, performance-claim restrictions, fee-transparency requirements, required risk disclosures.
- Healthcare: PHI handling, HIPAA-aware form and storage requirements, patient-privacy notice presence, telehealth consent where applicable.
- Consulting: client-confidentiality handling in case studies, absence of fabricated metrics, standard data-privacy items — the lightest regulatory load of the four.
- All verticals: cookie/tracking consent and accessibility conformance sections are shared; only advertising, privacy and records sections vary.

## Acceptance checks
1. Every checklist item is a real `<input type="checkbox">` with a bound `<label>`.
2. Each item's reason text sits in reading order next to its label, not hover-only.
3. Section headings follow a logical, sequential order.
4. Checkbox state persists across a page reload within the same session.
5. The document states explicitly, in its own text, that it is build guidance and not legal advice.
6. No vertical-specific disclaimer or disclosure wording is invented — every such slot is marked client/counsel-supplied.
7. Focus-visible outlines and touch targets meet the stated contrast and size minimums.
8. No motion is present anywhere on the surface.

title: Consulting Firm Site
our_text:
# Consulting Firm Site

Complete homepage for a boutique B2B consulting firm at SMB scale (2–20 consultants, one or more sector focuses). The job is credibility and a clear path to a first conversation — capabilities, sector fit, named people, and engagement structure, done without inventing proof this firm hasn't earned. Done means a working `/` route built on the S4 skeleton (`zs-s4-skeleton`) where a prospect can tell what the firm does, who they'd work with, how engagements are structured, and how to start a conversation.

## Structure

1. **Header** — firm name, primary CTA `Schedule a Call`, contact link.
2. **Hero** — capability promise in plain language, primary action contact, one credibility marker (sector focus or years active, not an invented statistic).
3. **Capabilities & sector band** — service lines and industries served, a light proof band rather than a licensure credentials band.
4. **Capabilities grid** — service lines, each linking to a detail page.
5. **Named consultants** — team preview linking to the full directory.
6. **Engagement models** — how work is structured (project, retainer, fractional).
7. **Case studies** — challenge, approach, outcome, handled without fabricated metrics or unauthorized logos.
8. **Contact / consultation block** — schedule-a-call entry point and a direct contact form.
9. **Footer** — firm name, contact, links, legal.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Single column at mobile; capabilities grid and consultant preview move 1 → 2 → 3 columns; case studies stack full-width at every size — a case study reads as a short narrative, not a card grid, and compressing it undersells the one piece of real proof this vertical has. Header CTA stays visible and un-collapsed at every width.

## Typography

Modular scale, 1.25 ratio, base 16px. Display for the hero promise, heading for section titles, body for paragraphs (16–18px, 45–75ch), label for nav/captions. Consulting copy can run slightly more editorial than the other three S4 verticals, but headings stay declarative, not adjective-stacked — state what the firm does, don't sell it.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--ink` (≥4.5:1), `--accent` (≥4.5:1 as text, ≥3:1 as a UI boundary), `--muted` (≥4.5:1), `--border` (≥3:1). No colour is hardcoded; the client's palette fills every token.

## Components

**Capability card** — name, one-line description, link to detail. States: default, hover, focus-visible.
**Consultant card** — photo, name, role/focus, link to profile. Credential claims (e.g. "PMP," "PhD") appear only when client-supplied and verifiable — omit the line rather than leave it implied.
**Engagement model card** — model name, what it means in one paragraph, what a prospect should expect to provide. No pricing figure unless the client supplies one.
**Case study card** — client (named with permission, or anonymized by sector/size), challenge, approach, outcome. States: default, hover/focus if linking to a full write-up, and an "anonymized" variant that never implies a name the client hasn't approved.

## Content slots

Firm name, tagline, capability list `[Capability — 1 sentence]`, sector list, consultant bios `[Name — role/focus]`, engagement-model descriptions, case-study fields each marked with a permission status (`[Named with permission]` / `[Anonymized — sector, size]`), optional testimonial slot `[Client testimonial — 2 sentences, client-supplied]`. Placeholders must read as obviously fake, never a plausible client name or number.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, restrained state feedback only. ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, hover and focus-visible feedback on cards and the CTA. No scroll choreography, autoplay video, or WebGL. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the transitions rather than shortening them.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible focus ring on every interactive element. Logical heading order, one H1. Contact form fields carry a programmatically associated `<label>` and error text (`aria-describedby`). Touch targets ≥44×44px. Contrast: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI boundaries. Keyboard path: skip link → header nav and CTA → hero CTA → each section in order → contact form fields → footer.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading/CTA pair — name it per build. Images (consultant photos, case-study imagery) ship with explicit dimensions, `loading="lazy"` except the named LCP candidate. No layout shift from webfonts (`font-display: swap`, matched fallback metrics). No scheduling-widget script loads render-blocking above the fold.

## Vertical adaptation

- Consulting carries no licensure regime and no mandated disclaimer, so the generic S4 credentials band compresses into a lighter capabilities-and-sector-focus band. Do not manufacture a compliance section that doesn't apply here just to match the other three verticals.
- **Restraint here is a deliberate choice, not a legal requirement.** The S4 trust-clinical posture — plain hero copy, no motion, sober colour use — still applies, but because it is what makes a boutique advisory firm read as senior and credible, not because a regulator requires it. State this to whoever builds the site, so the brief isn't loosened just because nothing forces it to stay tight.
- Case studies replace testimonials as the primary proof type. Every outcome is either a verified, client-approved figure with its source noted, or a non-numeric outcome statement — never an invented percentage or dollar figure filled in to complete a template.
- Client names and logos in a case study require a documented permission record on file; the default published state is anonymized by sector and size band until the client signs off on named attribution.
- Engagement-model clarity substitutes for the anxiety-reduction job a "what to expect" process section does for the regulated verticals — a consulting prospect's hesitation is about fit and cost structure, not compliance, so this section should answer "how would this actually work" plainly.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Every case study outcome is either a verified, client-approved figure with its source noted, or a non-numeric statement — no invented percentage or dollar amount exists anywhere.
- [ ] No client logo appears without a documented permission record; unattributed case studies use sector/size anonymization only.
- [ ] Capabilities/proof band shows only what the firm can substantiate — no licensure or regulatory claim is implied.
- [ ] Engagement models are described in plain terms a prospect could paraphrase back correctly.
- [ ] Motion stays within the same ≤150ms hover/focus budget as the rest of the S4 kit despite the lighter compliance load.
- [ ] Every colour reference in code is a `--token`, none a literal hex/rgb value.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass reaches every interactive element with a visible focus ring.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all transitions when tested.
- [ ] Named LCP element loads with `fetchpriority="high"`.
- [ ] Consultant cards show name and focus area at minimum; any credential claim is client-supplied and verifiable, never assumed.

title: Credentials & Licensure Band
our_text:
# Credentials & Licensure Band

This band sits directly under the hero defined in the S4 homepage skeleton (`zs-s4-skeleton`) and is the single highest-trust element on a professional services page. It displays licences, bar admissions, board certifications, registrations, and professional memberships as design elements, not fine print. Done means every credential shown is honestly scoped — jurisdiction and currency stated, nothing implied that the client hasn't supplied evidence for.

## Structure

1. **Section label (optional)** — e.g. "Licensed and Certified," present only if the band needs framing; many builds run it unlabelled directly under the hero.
2. **Credential items** — a row or grid of individual credentials, each self-contained (name, issuing body, jurisdiction, status).
3. **Verification note (optional)** — a short line pointing to where a visitor can independently verify a licence, when the client wants it.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Mobile: single column list or a horizontally scrollable row with visible scroll affordance, never a hidden carousel. Tablet: 2-column grid. Desktop: 3–4 column grid, or a single row if the count is 4 or fewer. Layout must not look sparse at 2 items or crowded at 8 — wrap, don't shrink text to fit.

## Typography

Credential name uses the label role, 500 weight. Issuing body and jurisdiction use a smaller caption size in `--muted`. No credential text uses the display role — this band is confirmation, not a headline. Line length per item stays short; wrap rather than truncate.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (band background, may differ subtly from the page surface), `--ink` (credential name, ≥4.5:1), `--muted` (issuing body, jurisdiction, status, ≥4.5:1), `--border` (dividers or the band's rule, ≥3:1), `--accent` only if an icon needs a boundary colour, never as a fill here. No brand colour is hardcoded.

## Components

**Credential item** — optional small mark/icon (a generic seal, never a fabricated official emblem), credential name, issuing body, jurisdiction, optional status tag (`Active`, `Since [year]`). States: default and focus-visible only if the item links out; non-linking items must not look clickable. Loading state (CMS-fed builds) is a static skeleton, no shimmer. Error state hides the band rather than showing a broken item. Empty state means the band does not render — never padded with placeholders.

## Content slots

Per credential: name, issuing body, jurisdiction, status and expiry date if the client wants it shown, optional verification link. Mark every slot `[Client-supplied: <what>]`. Draft placeholders must be obviously fake, e.g. `[Licence type — jurisdiction]`, never a real-sounding bar number.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: static. Only the kit-wide hover/focus feedback applies, and only if an item is a link (≤150ms, opacity or transform only). No entrance animation, no counting-up effect on any numeric credential, no scroll-triggered reveal. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` makes any linked item's state change instant.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Each credential is a list item (`<ul>`/`<li>`) so assistive tech announces the count. Linking items carry a visible focus ring and a ≥44×44px hit area. Icons are `aria-hidden="true"` with the credential name carrying the accessible text. Contrast: 4.5:1 for name and issuing body, 3:1 for any divider.

## Performance

Renders as static server content — no client-side fetch blocks first paint. Icons ship as inline SVG or a single sprite, not individual image requests. Not an LCP candidate by design; if it lands above the fold on a short hero, confirm it doesn't outsize the hero and become the LCP element unintentionally.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** bar admissions per state/jurisdiction, and years admitted if shown. Never imply authority to practice in a jurisdiction the credential doesn't cover.
- **Financial advisory:** registrations (e.g. RIA) and designations (CFP, CFA); state plainly that a designation is not a guarantee of performance.
- **Medical/dental:** board certification and state licence; jurisdiction limit matters most — a licence valid in one state must not imply practice rights elsewhere.
- **Consulting:** memberships and certifications carry less regulatory weight; still state issuing body and date so nothing reads as self-declared.
- Across all four: expired or lapsed credentials are removed, never left displayed with a silently outdated date.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Band renders directly under the hero, above the practice areas grid.
- [ ] Every credential states issuing body and jurisdiction, not just a name.
- [ ] No credential implies validity outside its stated jurisdiction.
- [ ] No numeric credential animates or counts up on load.
- [ ] Items are marked up as a list; screen reader announces the item count.
- [ ] Any linked item shows a visible focus ring and meets the 44×44px target.
- [ ] Icons, if present, are `aria-hidden` and never the sole carrier of meaning.
- [ ] Band does not render when the credential list is empty.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` produces instant state changes on any linked item.

title: Financial Advisory Site
our_text:
# Financial Advisory Site

A complete homepage for an independent financial advisory or wealth-management firm, built to move a visitor to a booked consultation without implying a return, a guarantee, or an undisclosed fiduciary duty. The S4 skeleton bent by financial-promotion rules: every claim about performance, cost, or duty is sourced, disclosed, or cut.

## Structure

1. Header — firm name, services menu, phone, "Schedule a consultation".
2. Hero — client served and problem solved, CTA to book.
3. Registration/fiduciary band — registration, ADV/CRS link, fiduciary status.
4. Services grid — planning, investment management, tax, retirement.
5. Advisor profiles — credentials (CFP, CFA, etc.), links to `/team/{slug}`.
6. Fee model — how the firm is paid, plain language.
7. Client journey — discovery call → plan → onboarding → review.
8. Testimonials, gated by marketing-rule conditions.
9. Consultation booking + secure-contact entry.
10. Footer — registration numbers, disclosures, ADV/CRS links.

Routes: `/` `/practice-areas` `/practice/{slug}` `/team` `/team/{slug}` `/booking` `/intake` `/resources` `/contact` `/thank-you`.

## Layout & responsive

Single column under 640px, phone pinned in the collapsed header. 640–1024px: two-column grids, fee model stacks. 1024px+: three-column grids, sticky header. Registration band and fee figures stay adjacent to their disclosure.

## Typography

Display 2.25rem/2.75rem, body 1rem/1.125rem at 1.6 line-height, label 0.875rem. Modular scale ×1.25. Body capped at 70ch. Disclosure text is never lighter-weight than body.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--ink`, `--ink-muted`, `--accent`, `--border`, `--focus-ring`. Body ≥4.5:1; `--accent` ≥3:1. Fee or return figures use `--ink`, never `--ink-muted`.

## Components

- **Hero**: headline, subhead, single CTA. States: default, focus-visible.
- **Registration band**: repeatable item (type, number, jurisdiction, verify link), static.
- **Service card**: title, description, link. States: hover, focus-visible, active; whole card is the link.
- **Advisor card**: photo, name, designations, focus area, link.
- **Fee block**: structure named (AUM %, flat, hourly, commission), minimum if any. Default only.
- **Testimonial item**: disclosure renders with the item, where permitted.
- **Intake form**: contact and topic only, pre-engagement. States: default, validating, error, submitting, success.
- **Booking widget**: type, availability. States: loading, error, no-availability, confirmed.

## Content slots

`[Firm name]`, `[Service + 1–2 sentence description]` ×3–10, `[Advisor name, designations, registration]`, `[Fee structure, plain terms]`, `[Testimonial — where counsel permits, obviously placeholder]`. Every figure is client-supplied and verifiable.

## Interaction & motion

Avoid motion. Hover/focus feedback only, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. No scrolljacking, WebGL, autoplay video, or animated counters. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes transition and transform, never shortens them.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible keyboard focus everywhere, logical heading order, controls labelled with `aria-describedby` error association, touch targets ≥44×44px, contrast as above. Keyboard path: nav → hero → registration band → services → advisors → fee model → booking/intake; disclosure in the same tab order as its figure.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero headline. Advisor photography ships with explicit width/height, `loading="lazy"` below the fold. No webfont shift — `font-display: swap` with matched fallbacks. Booking loads off critical path.

## Vertical adaptation

- Fiduciary status is fact, not marketing: a fee-only fiduciary shows the registration proving it; commission-based firms state that plainly.
- No performance figure or "typical result" appears without a dated source and risk disclosure beside it.
- Testimonials follow counsel-set conditions (compensation disclosure, no cherry-picking); hideable per firm.
- Fee transparency is structural: its own section, not a footer link.
- Any calculator carries an inline "hypothetical, not a guarantee" label at output.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Registration/fiduciary band renders in the first scroll, not buried in the footer.
- [ ] No dollar figure, percentage, or return claim appears without an adjacent, visible disclosure.
- [ ] Fee model is a dedicated section, reachable from primary nav.
- [ ] Testimonial module can be fully disabled per firm without a layout gap.
- [ ] Intake form collects only contact and topic pre-engagement — no account detail before a relationship exists.
- [ ] All CTAs and controls reach by keyboard; contrast meets 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large text on disclosure text.
- [ ] Reduced-motion removes, not shortens, all transitions; no animated counters anywhere.
- [ ] No testimonial or return figure is invented — all use marked bracket slots.
- [ ] Build guidance only; the firm's compliance counsel signs off before launch.

title: Professional Services Hero
our_text:
# Professional Services Hero

The above-the-fold opener sitting directly under the shared header defined in the S4 homepage skeleton (`zs-s4-skeleton`). It is the first thing a prospective client reads, often under real stress or real stakes. Done means a calm, plain-language promise, one immediate action, and one credibility marker — nothing promotional, nothing that reads as a sales pitch.

## Structure

1. **Eyebrow (optional)** — practice area or specialism, one short label.
2. **Practice promise** — H1, plain language, what the firm does and for whom.
3. **Supporting line** — one sentence expanding the promise, no unverifiable adjectives.
4. **Primary CTA** — `Book a Consultation`, links to `/booking`.
5. **Secondary action** — phone as a `tel:` link, or plain text if the practice screens contact through intake.
6. **Credibility marker** — one verifiable line: years in practice, a membership, a jurisdiction/licence. Not a review count or client logo wall.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Single column, text-first, at every width. An optional supporting image (office, provider, or abstract mark — never a stock "handshake" photo) sits below the text on mobile and beside it from tablet up, at a fixed aspect ratio so it never shifts layout while loading. No full-bleed background video.

## Typography

Practice promise uses the display role, top of the modular scale (1.25 ratio, base 16px) — large but not oversized, read as a statement rather than a headline shout. Supporting line and credibility marker use body scale; CTA label uses label role at 500 weight. Supporting line stays within 45–75 characters; the promise caps at roughly two lines at desktop.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (background), `--ink` (promise/supporting text, ≥4.5:1), `--accent` (CTA fill or border, ≥3:1, ≥4.5:1 as text), `--muted` (eyebrow/marker, ≥4.5:1), `--border` (rule between text and image, ≥3:1). No brand colour is named or hardcoded.

## Components

**Primary CTA button** — states: default, hover (opacity/background shift, ≤150ms), focus-visible (2px ring, ≥3:1), active (pressed, ≤150ms). Minimum 44×44px hit area.

**Phone link** — plain `tel:` anchor styled as a secondary action, not competing with the CTA. Tap-to-call on mobile; a visible, selectable number on desktop, never icon-only.

**Credibility marker** — static text or a small inline badge. No animation, no counter that increments on load.

## Content slots

Eyebrow (optional, ≤4 words), practice promise (≤14 words), supporting line (1 sentence), phone number, credibility marker (1 line, verifiable fact only), optional hero image with descriptive alt text. Mark every slot `[Client-supplied: <what>]`. If no verified credential exists yet, the marker ships as `[Credential or years-in-practice — client to confirm]`, never a filled-in guess.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, per the S4 kit. Only hover/focus/active feedback on the CTA and phone link, ≤150ms, opacity or transform only. No entrance animation, scroll-triggered reveal, or autoplay media. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` shows state changes instantly rather than shortening the transition.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. The practice promise is the page's single H1. CTA and phone link carry visible focus rings and ≥44×44px targets. Hero image alt text describes content, not decoration. Contrast: 4.5:1 for promise, supporting line, and credibility marker; 3:1 for the CTA's border/fill. Keyboard path: header → eyebrow (if focusable) → CTA → phone link → next section.

## Performance

The practice promise or the hero image — whichever renders first — is the named LCP element; confirm it with `fetchpriority="high"` and no lazy-loading. Any hero image ships with explicit `width`/`height`. No webfont swap reflows the promise after first paint. No third-party script loads above this section.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** promise names the practice area plainly; marker is a bar admission or years-admitted, never a case outcome.
- **Financial advisory:** promise avoids performance language; marker is a registration or fiduciary statement, not assets-under-management framed as skill.
- **Medical/dental:** promise is patient-facing and plain; marker is board certification, not a satisfaction percentage.
- **Consulting:** least restricted — promise can name outcomes generally, marker can be years or sector focus, never an invented metric.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Hero renders directly under the shared header with no region between them.
- [ ] Exactly one H1 exists and it is the practice promise.
- [ ] Primary CTA links to `/booking`; phone link is a working `tel:` anchor.
- [ ] Credibility marker is a verifiable fact type, never a fabricated statistic.
- [ ] No animation exceeds 150ms or touches a property other than opacity/transform.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` produces instant state changes when tested.
- [ ] CTA and phone link meet 44×44px minimum with a visible focus ring on tab.
- [ ] Named LCP element loads with `fetchpriority="high"`.
- [ ] No hero image causes layout shift on load.

title: Compliance-Aware Intake Form
our_text:
# Compliance-Aware Intake Form

For law, financial advisory, medical and consulting firms collecting matter or case detail before an engagement starts. Job: triage a lead without collecting privileged or protected information prematurely, hand off cleanly to a CRM, and never lose a client's typed answers to a timeout. Done = a screen-reader user, a keyboard-only user and a user on a shaky connection can all complete it unaided.

## Structure
1. Step indicator — current step, total steps, step names.
2. Step 1: Contact & matter type.
3. Step 2: Details — matter-specific fields, conditional on practice area.
4. Step 3: Conflict-check or equivalent screening fields.
5. Step 4: Consent & privacy — data-use notice, consent checkbox(es), file upload.
6. Step 5: Review & submit — summary, edit links to each step.
7. Confirmation — next steps, expected response time, no promise of engagement.

## Layout & responsive
Single column at all breakpoints (<640px, 640–1024px, >1024px) — reflow only adds mis-tab risk. Field width caps at 640px on desktop, centered. Buttons stack full-width on mobile, inline right-aligned on desktop.

## Typography
Labels: label role, 14–16px, weight 500–600, always visible, never placeholder-as-label. Help text: body role, 14–15px, max 65 characters/line. Field values: 16px minimum (prevents iOS zoom-on-focus). Step heading: display-small.

## Colour & tokens
`--surface` (4.5:1 vs `--ink`), `--ink` (text, 4.5:1), `--border` (field borders, 3:1), `--accent` (active step, focus ring, button, 3:1), `--error` (invalid state, 4.5:1), `--muted` (help text, 4.5:1). Error never relies on colour alone.

## Components
- Step indicator: ordered list, current step `aria-current="step"`. States: upcoming, current, complete.
- Fields: visible `<label>` bound via `for`/`id`. States: default, focus-visible, filled, invalid (inline error), disabled.
- File upload: native `<input type="file">` behind a styled trigger, drag-and-drop as enhancement only. States: empty, selected, uploading (cancelable), error, success.
- Consent checkbox: required, linked to the privacy notice, never pre-checked.
- Navigation: Back, Next, Submit. Next disables until the step validates; disabled state stays keyboard-reachable and announces why.
- Review screen: read-only summary by step, each with an "Edit" link that returns focus there.

## Content slots
Practice-area options `[Client-supplied list]`. Field labels/help text per vertical `[Firm-supplied]`. Privacy notice body `[Firm's actual policy text — never placeholder legal language]`. Confirmation copy and response time `[Client-supplied]` — never invent a commitment.

## Interaction & motion
Motion budget: micro. Step transitions use opacity fade ≤150ms only, no slide/translate, no scroll animation. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the fade — step change is instant.

## Accessibility
- Every control has a visible, programmatically associated `<label>` (`for`/`id` or `aria-labelledby`) — no placeholder-only labels.
- Validation errors link to their field with `aria-describedby` pointing at the error id; the field carries `aria-invalid="true"` while invalid.
- On step change, the new step's heading receives focus and the change is announced via a visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` region (e.g. "Step 2 of 5: Matter details").
- Form state saves on every step change — save-and-resume. Reopening restores entered values and the last completed step, announced on load.
- File upload is fully operable by keyboard alone (native input, no drag-only path), announces filename and size, and states rejection reasons as text, not colour or icon alone.
- No timing limit ever discards entered data. A mid-form session or CSRF expiry re-authenticates silently and preserves every field value — never blanks the form.
- All interactive elements meet 44×44px touch target and follow a single logical Tab sequence matching visual order.
- Contrast: 4.5:1 body text and labels, 3:1 borders, focus rings and other UI boundaries.

## Performance
LCP element is the step 1 heading or first field, no image. File upload and any CRM SDK load only when reached (code-split). `font-display: swap` with a matched fallback prevents webfont shift. Submission runs through server actions.

## Vertical adaptation
- Law: conflict-check fields mandatory; copy states this does not create an attorney-client relationship.
- Financial advisory: "matter type" becomes service type; net-worth/risk fields only if compliance requires them.
- Medical/dental: upload doubles as insurance/referral upload; HIPAA-aware privacy slot; confirmation avoids implying a confirmed appointment.
- Consulting: drop the conflict-check step ("not applicable"); keep engagement-type and budget fields.
- All verticals: nothing beyond name, contact and matter category is collected before consent.

## Acceptance checks
1. Every field has a visible label programmatically bound to its input.
2. Every validation error is linked via `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid`.
3. Step changes move focus to the new heading and announce via `aria-live`.
4. Reloading mid-form restores entered values and the last step reached.
5. File upload is completable using keyboard only, no drag-and-drop dependency.
6. No session or token expiry clears entered field data.
7. All touch targets measure at least 44×44px.
8. Body text meets 4.5:1 contrast; borders and focus rings meet 3:1.
9. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the step-transition fade entirely.
10. No field before consent collects matter-privileged detail.

title: Law Firm Site
our_text:
# Law Firm Site

A complete homepage for a small or mid-size law firm, built to convert a visitor with a legal problem into a booked consultation without breaching attorney-advertising rules. This is the S4 skeleton bent for legal: no outcome implied as typical or guaranteed, no advice given pre-engagement, and intake never collects privileged detail before a conflict check clears.

## Structure

1. Header — firm name, practice menu, phone, "Schedule a consultation".
2. Hero — the problem solved, CTA to book, CTA to call.
3. Credentials band — bar admissions, years practicing, memberships.
4. Practice areas grid — links to `/practice/{slug}`.
5. Attorney profiles — featured, links to `/team/{slug}`.
6. Case-result module — outcomes as illustrative, disclaimer inline.
7. Client journey — consultation → engagement letter → representation.
8. Testimonials, gated per jurisdiction rule.
9. Booking + conflict-aware intake entry.
10. Footer — bar admissions, advertising notice, jurisdictions, disclaimer.

Routes: `/` `/practice-areas` `/practice/{slug}` `/team` `/team/{slug}` `/booking` `/intake` `/resources` `/contact` `/thank-you`.

## Layout & responsive

Single column under 640px, header collapses with phone pinned visible. 640–1024px: two-column grids. 1024px+: three-column grids, sticky header. Case results and testimonials never carousel — a result stays visible with its disclaimer.

## Typography

Display 2.25rem/2.75rem, body 1rem/1.125rem at 1.6 line-height, label 0.875rem. Modular scale ×1.25. Body capped at 70ch. Disclaimers never sit below label size.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--ink`, `--ink-muted`, `--accent`, `--border`, `--focus-ring`. Body ≥4.5:1 on `--surface`; `--accent` ≥3:1. Disclaimer text uses `--ink`, never `--ink-muted`.

## Components

- **Hero**: headline, subhead, dual CTA. States: default, focus-visible.
- **Credentials band**: repeatable item (credential, issuer, jurisdiction), static.
- **Practice card**: title, description, link. States: hover, focus-visible, active; whole card is the link.
- **Attorney card**: photo, name, bar admissions, focus area, link.
- **Case-result item**: matter type, outcome, disclaimer in the same node, never a tooltip.
- **Intake form**: multi-step, conflict-check first, upload. States: default, validating, error, submitting, success, save-and-resume.
- **Booking widget**: type, duration, availability. States: loading, error, no-availability, confirmed.

## Content slots

`[Firm name]`, `[Practice area + 1–2 sentence description]` ×3–20, `[Attorney name, admissions, jurisdictions, education]`, `[Case result — outcome only, no client detail without consent]`, `[Testimonial — where permitted, obviously placeholder]`. Every credential is client-supplied and verifiable.

## Interaction & motion

Avoid motion. Hover/focus feedback only, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only. No scrolljacking, WebGL, or autoplay video. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes transition and transform — never shortens them.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible keyboard focus everywhere, logical heading order, controls labelled with `aria-describedby` error association, touch targets ≥44×44px, contrast as above. Keyboard path: nav → hero → practice grid → attorney grid → case results → intake/booking. No trap in the form; steps announced via `aria-live`.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero headline. Attorney photography ships with explicit width/height, `loading="lazy"` below the fold. No webfont shift — `font-display: swap` with matched fallbacks. Booking and review widgets load off the critical path.

## Vertical adaptation

- Case results carry a "past results don't predict a future outcome" disclaimer inline every time, never once at page bottom.
- Testimonials are gated per state bar rule — some jurisdictions restrict or ban endorsements; the build supports hiding the module per firm.
- Intake collects contact and matter-type only until conflict-check clears; privileged fields stay locked, not merely labeled confidential.
- Footer states the exact jurisdictions each attorney is admitted in — a credential, not boilerplate; "free consultation" states what is covered.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Every case result renders its disclaimer in the same visible block, not a hidden tooltip.
- [ ] Testimonial module can be fully disabled per firm without a layout gap.
- [ ] Intake form blocks privileged-detail fields until conflict-check fields are complete.
- [ ] Every attorney card states bar admissions and jurisdiction.
- [ ] All CTAs and form controls are reachable by keyboard alone; contrast meets 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large text, verified on disclaimer text.
- [ ] Reduced-motion removes, not shortens, all transitions.
- [ ] No testimonial or case outcome is invented — all use marked bracket slots.
- [ ] Build guidance only; the firm's bar-licensed counsel signs off on advertising compliance before launch.

title: Medical Practice Site
our_text:
# Medical Practice Site

Complete homepage for a private medical or dental practice at SMB scale (2–15 providers, one or two locations). The job is credibility, provider trust, and appointment booking, done without turning the marketing site into a clinical data-collection tool. Done means a working `/` route built on the S4 skeleton (`zs-s4-skeleton`) where a visitor finds the right provider, understands what insurance is accepted, and calls or requests an appointment — and nothing on the page asks for information that belongs behind an authenticated patient portal instead.

## Structure

1. **Header** — practice name, phone, primary CTA `Book an Appointment`, separate `Patient Portal` link (outbound, authenticated elsewhere).
2. **Hero** — practice promise in plain language, primary action book/call, one credibility marker (e.g. practice accreditation).
3. **Credentials band** — board certifications, state licensure, practice accreditation, insurance networks accepted.
4. **Conditions & treatments grid** — service lines, each linking to a detail page.
5. **Provider directory preview** — 3–4 featured clinicians linking to the full directory.
6. **Insurance & payment info** — accepted carriers, self-pay policy, financial-assistance note if offered.
7. **Patient journey** — what a new patient does from first contact to first visit.
8. **Testimonials with compliance handling** — satisfaction rating and/or consented, platform-sourced quotes only.
9. **Appointment booking block** — non-clinical request form, with the patient portal kept as a separate, clearly distinct path.
10. **Contact & locations** — address, hours, map.
11. **Footer** — NAP, licences, Notice of Privacy Practices link, non-discrimination notice, accessibility statement.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Single column at mobile; conditions grid and provider preview move 1 → 2 → 3 columns; credentials band becomes a horizontally scrollable row on mobile with visible scroll affordance. Header phone and both CTAs (`Book`, `Patient Portal`) stay visible at every width — never collapsed behind the mobile nav disclosure.

## Typography

Modular scale, 1.25 ratio, base 16px. Display for the hero promise, heading for section titles, body for paragraphs (16–18px, 45–75ch), label for nav/form fields/captions. Condition and treatment names lead in plain language ("Knee pain," not only "Osteoarthritis, knee"); a clinical term may follow in parentheses, never replace the plain heading.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface`, `--ink` (≥4.5:1), `--accent` (≥4.5:1 as text, ≥3:1 as a UI boundary), `--muted` (≥4.5:1), `--border` (≥3:1), `--success` for an "insurance accepted" chip. No colour is hardcoded; the client's palette fills every token — avoid defaulting to a generic clinical blue/green, that is a house-aesthetic shortcut, not this client's identity.

## Components

**Provider card** — photo, name, credentials, board certification, one focus line, link to profile. States: default, hover, focus-visible, "joining soon" (no booking link).
**Condition/treatment card** — name, one-line description, link to detail. Same state set.
**Insurance list** — carrier chips, `--success` for accepted, `--muted` for "call to confirm." No eligibility checker on this site.
**Appointment request form** — fields defined under Vertical adaptation. States: default, per-field focus-visible, inline error tied to its field, submitting (disabled button, no spinner-only state), success confirmation, failure that preserves entered values.

## Content slots

Practice name, tagline, per-condition description `[Condition — 1 plain-language sentence]`, provider bios `[Provider name — credentials, focus]`, accepted-insurance list, hours, address, phone, patient portal URL, Notice of Privacy Practices link, accreditation marks (only with confirmed usage rights), testimonial slot `[Patient testimonial — consented, 2 sentences]`. Placeholders must read as obviously fake, never a plausible patient quote.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, restrained state feedback only. ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, hover and focus-visible feedback on cards and the booking CTA. No scroll choreography, autoplay video, or WebGL. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the transitions rather than shortening them.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible focus ring on every interactive element. Logical heading order, one H1. Appointment-request fields carry a programmatically associated `<label>` and error text (`aria-describedby`), announced without a full-page reload. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Contrast: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI boundaries. Keyboard path: skip link → header (phone, book, portal) → hero CTA → each section in order → booking form fields → footer.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading/CTA pair — name it per build; a hero photograph, if used instead, ships with explicit dimensions and `fetchpriority="high"`. No layout shift from webfonts (`font-display: swap`, matched fallback metrics). The patient-portal link is a plain outbound link, never an embedded iframe.

## Vertical adaptation

- **The defining constraint is what this site must not collect.** The appointment-request form takes name, phone, email, preferred date/time, insurance carrier name, and a reason picked from a fixed list ("New patient," "Follow-up," "Specific concern — will discuss by phone") — never free-text symptoms. It must not collect a Social Security number, full date of birth beyond age-based routing, insurance member/policy ID, diagnosis, medication list, or any photo or narrative of a condition. Anything clinical routes to a phone call or the authenticated patient portal, outside this build.
- The patient portal is a labelled outbound link, never an embedded login form — no clinical credential ever touches this codebase.
- Provider credentials are shown per-provider, not just per-practice: a patient chooses a clinician, not a brand.
- Testimonials lean toward an aggregate satisfaction rating over quotes, since a quote can inadvertently disclose a condition; any quote requires documented patient consent tracked outside this codebase.
- **This is build guidance for a marketing website, not legal or compliance advice.** It does not determine what counts as protected health information or which rules apply to this practice — confirm with the client's own counsel or compliance officer before launch.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Appointment-request form has only name, phone, email, preferred date/time, insurance carrier, and a pick-list reason — no free-text symptom field anywhere.
- [ ] No field requests SSN, full DOB beyond routing needs, insurance member ID, or diagnosis.
- [ ] Patient portal is a labelled outbound link, never an embedded login iframe.
- [ ] Every provider card states board certification and licensing jurisdiction.
- [ ] Testimonials show only an aggregate rating or a consented, attributed quote.
- [ ] Insurance section lists accepted carriers only; no eligibility checker transmits patient identifiers.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass reaches the booking form, submits, and receives an accessible confirmation.
- [ ] Every colour reference in code is a `--token`, none a literal hex/rgb value.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all transitions when tested.
- [ ] Named LCP element loads with `fetchpriority="high"`.

title: Practice Areas Grid
our_text:
# Practice Areas Grid

A grid that lets a visitor find the right practice area in one glance and one click. It
serves two very different firms with the same component: a three-partner practice with
three areas, and a regional firm with twenty. "Done" means both firms ship this without
custom layout work, and a visitor self-identifies into the correct area before they read
past the fold.

## Structure

1. Section heading — names the firm's areas of practice as a category, not a slogan.
2. Optional grouping controls — present only above a stated item count (see Layout).
3. Area grid — one card per practice area, each a full-card link to `/practice/{slug}`.
4. Overflow or "view all" path — for firms whose full list exceeds the default grid.

## Layout & responsive

- Mobile (< 640px): single column, full-width cards, no grouping controls shown.
- Tablet (640–1024px): two columns.
- Desktop (≥ 1024px): three columns up to 9 areas; four columns beyond that.
- At 10+ areas, group cards under subheadings (e.g. by department) rather than growing
  an unbroken grid — subheadings are `<h3>` under the section `<h2>`.
- Card height is intrinsic to content; no forced equal-height grid that clips text.
  Use CSS Grid `align-items: start` so uneven card copy never stretches or truncates.
- Nothing reflows on resize beyond column count; card internal layout is stable.

## Typography

- Section heading: display role, step 4 on a 1.25 modular scale.
- Card title (area name): step 2, semibold. One line at desktop width; wraps at mobile.
- Card description: body role, step 0, 2–3 lines, clamped with visible affordance
  (no silent truncation — end in a complete clause or add "Learn more").
- Optional group subheading: label role, step 1, uppercase or letter-spaced, not both.
- Line length for card description: 45–75 characters measured at the card's own width.

## Colour & tokens

- `--surface`: card background, contrast 3:1 against `--surface-page` (page background)
  so cards read as distinct regions.
- `--ink`: card title and body text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
- `--muted`: card description and metadata, 4.5:1 against `--surface` (body-text ratio
  applies even to secondary copy).
- `--accent`: card border or icon accent on hover/focus, 3:1 against `--surface`.
- `--border`: default card border, 3:1 against `--surface`.

## Components

**Area card**
- Structure: icon or initials mark (optional), area name, one-line description,
  optional metadata (e.g. "12 attorneys" or "Est. 1998" if client supplies it).
- Content slots: `area_name` (required), `area_description` (1 sentence,
  ≤140 characters), `icon` (optional, client-supplied or omitted — never a stock
  generic icon set implying a specialism the firm didn't confirm).
- States: default; hover (border/accent shift, ≤150ms); focus-visible (2px outline,
  offset, meets 3:1 against `--surface`); active (pressed, no layout shift); the whole
  card is the single link target, `<a>` wrapping the card content, not a button
  inside a non-interactive card.

**Grouping toggle (10+ areas only)**
- Structure: a `<select>` or button group offering "By department" / "A–Z".
- States: default, focus-visible, selected. Client decides default order; if firms
  supply no revenue-weighting data, default to alphabetical — never guess an order
  that implies priority the firm didn't state.

## Content slots

- `area_name` — required, ≤40 characters, matches the firm's own naming, not ours.
- `area_description` — required, ≤140 characters, one sentence, plain language.
- `icon` — optional, client-supplied SVG or omitted entirely.
- `metadata` — optional (attorney count, years active) — client-supplied only.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, per S4. Hover and focus-visible feedback only: border-colour or
background shift, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, no card lift or shadow animation.
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the transition entirely (instant state change),
it does not merely shorten it. No scroll-triggered reveal on this grid.

## Accessibility

- Grid is a `<nav>` or a `<ul>` of links, never a `<div>` soup — screen readers must
  announce "N links" or "N items."
- Each card link has an accessible name equal to the area name; description text is
  associated, not a separate unlabeled paragraph screen readers skip.
- Keyboard path: Tab moves card to card in visual order; Enter activates the link
  under focus; grouping toggle (if present) is a native `<select>` or ARIA-compliant
  button group, reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
- Touch targets ≥44×44px including the full card, not just the title text.
- Colour contrast: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 card borders and focus outline.

## Performance

- This section is not typically the LCP element (hero usually is); if it is the LCP
  candidate on a practice-areas index page, name the first card's title text as the
  LCP element and avoid a client-fetched icon blocking its paint.
- Icons, if used, are inline SVG or a single sprite sheet — no per-card icon-font
  request. No layout shift: reserve icon dimensions in markup.
- Grid renders server-side; no client component needed unless the grouping toggle is
  present, in which case only the toggle is a client component — the grid itself
  stays server-rendered and re-orders via CSS or a server action, not client re-fetch.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** areas are practice groups (e.g. "Family Law," "Estate Planning"); card
  copy avoids outcome language per advertising rules — describe the service, not a
  result.
- **Financial advisory:** areas are service lines (e.g. "Retirement Planning");
  never pair an area card with a performance figure — that belongs behind disclosure,
  not on a grid card.
- **Medical/dental:** areas are conditions or treatments; card copy stays clinical,
  no before/after implication, no unverified outcome claims.
- **Consulting:** areas are capabilities or sectors; metadata can include client
  count only if the firm supplies a real, current figure — never a rounded guess.

## Acceptance checks

1. Grid renders correctly with 3 areas and with 20 areas without custom code changes.
2. At 10+ areas, cards are grouped under labelled subheadings, not one long grid.
3. Every card is a single `<a>` element with a complete accessible name.
4. Card description never truncates mid-word or mid-sentence.
5. Focus-visible outline is present on every card and meets 3:1 contrast.
6. Touch target for each card is ≥44×44px measured on the full card, not the text.
7. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes hover transitions, not just shortens them.
8. No area ordering implies firm priority unless the firm explicitly supplied it.
9. No icon or metadata appears that the client did not supply.
10. Grid is server-rendered; only the optional grouping toggle is a client component.

title: Practice Area Landing Template
our_text:
# Practice Area Landing Template

Template for `/practice/{slug}`, the page a visitor lands on from search or from the
practice-areas grid when they already know roughly what they need. It must answer, in
order, what the firm does in this area, who it's for, how the engagement works, and
what to do next. "Done" means this page can rank for the practice area's search terms
and convert a cold visitor into a booked consultation without them leaving the page.

## Structure

1. Breadcrumb — Home / Practice Areas / {area name}, for orientation and SEO.
2. Hero — area name, one-paragraph description of the service, primary intake CTA.
3. Who this serves — short list of client situations or profiles this area covers.
4. What the firm does — the scope of work in plain language, not a legal/clinical
   glossary dump.
5. Process — the steps from first contact to resolution (links to the shared Client
   Journey section where one exists, or repeats it briefly).
6. Typical outcomes — described qualitatively, never as a guarantee or statistic.
7. Assigned team — cards for the professionals who work this area, linking to
   `/team/{slug}`.
8. FAQ — 4–8 questions specific to this area.
9. Intake CTA — repeated, closing the page.

## Layout & responsive

- Mobile (< 640px): single column throughout; team cards stack; FAQ is an accordion.
- Tablet (640–1024px): team section becomes two columns; body content stays single
  column and full measure for readability.
- Desktop (≥ 1024px): optional sidebar (sticky CTA or "on this page" jump links)
  beside a single main content column; team section becomes three columns.
- Breadcrumb and CTA positions do not change across breakpoints; content order is
  identical at every width — only column count changes.

## Typography

- Area name (H1): display role, step 5.
- Section headings (H2): step 3, one per structural region above.
- Body copy: step 0, 60–75 character measure, regular weight.
- FAQ question: label-weight step 1; FAQ answer: body step 0.
- Team card name: step 2 semibold; credentials line: label role, step 0.

## Colour & tokens

- `--surface`: page and card background.
- `--ink`: headings and body text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
- `--muted`: metadata, breadcrumb, FAQ collapsed state text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
- `--accent`: CTA button and active/expanded FAQ indicator, 3:1 against `--surface`.
- `--border`: dividers between sections and around team cards, 3:1 against `--surface`.

## Components

**Intake CTA (hero and closing)**
- Structure: heading-adjacent button plus one supporting line ("Free 30-minute
  consultation" or firm-supplied equivalent).
- States: default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled (if booking is temporarily
  closed — must show why, not just grey out).

**Team card**
- Structure: photo, name, credential line, one-line focus statement, link to profile.
- Content slots: `name`, `credentials`, `focus_line` (≤100 characters), `photo`.
- States: default, hover (border shift only), focus-visible, and an empty state if
  no team member is yet assigned to this area (omit the section, don't show a
  placeholder card).

**FAQ accordion**
- Structure: question as a button, answer as a collapsible region.
- States: collapsed (default), expanded, focus-visible on the trigger button. Only
  client-supplied Q&A content — never a generated "common question" the firm hasn't
  reviewed for accuracy in their jurisdiction.

## Content slots

- `area_name`, `area_summary` (2–3 sentences), `who_its_for` (3–5 bullet points).
- `scope_of_work` (2–4 short paragraphs, plain language).
- `typical_outcomes` — qualitative description only; mark explicitly:
  `[Client-supplied — describe range of outcomes without guaranteeing a result]`.
- `team_assignments` — list of team slugs assigned to this area.
- `faq_items` — array of question/answer pairs, client-supplied and reviewed.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, per S4. FAQ expand/collapse uses a height or opacity transition
≤150ms, no easing beyond linear or ease-out. Hover/focus feedback only elsewhere.
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` makes the FAQ accordion open and close instantly with
no transition, rather than a shortened one. No parallax, no scroll-linked reveal.

## Accessibility

- Heading order is strictly H1 → H2 → H3; no skipped levels for visual sizing reasons.
- FAQ trigger buttons use `aria-expanded` and control a region referenced by
  `aria-controls`; state is announced to assistive tech on toggle.
- Breadcrumb is a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with an ordered list of links.
- Keyboard path: Tab reaches breadcrumb, hero CTA, each FAQ trigger in order, team
  card links, closing CTA — no element is reachable only by mouse.
- Touch targets ≥44×44px for CTA buttons and FAQ triggers.
- Colour contrast: 4.5:1 body and FAQ text, 3:1 CTA button boundary and focus ring.

## Performance

- LCP element is the hero heading (H1) or hero image if one is present — if an image
  is used, it ships with explicit `width`/`height` and `fetchpriority="high"`.
- Team card photos use `loading="lazy"` (below the fold) with explicit dimensions to
  prevent layout shift.
- Page is server-rendered; the FAQ accordion is the only client component, and it
  ships with no-JS fallback (details/summary or server-rendered expanded state).
- No third-party embed (chat widget, scheduler iframe) loads above the fold.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** "typical outcomes" must avoid any language a bar association would treat
  as a result guarantee; FAQ should address fee structure plainly (hourly vs flat).
- **Financial advisory:** no performance figures on this page; link out to the
  required disclosures page rather than restating them here.
- **Medical/dental:** "who this serves" reads as conditions/symptoms, not diagnoses;
  FAQ covers insurance and what a first visit involves.
- **Consulting:** "typical outcomes" can reference a named case study only if the
  client is named and has consented; otherwise keep it qualitative.

## Acceptance checks

1. Page renders all nine structural regions in the stated order at every breakpoint.
2. H1 contains the area name; no heading level is skipped anywhere on the page.
3. "Typical outcomes" copy contains no guarantee language or invented statistic.
4. Every FAQ trigger has correct `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` wiring.
5. Team section is omitted cleanly, not placeholder-filled, when no one is assigned.
6. Hero and closing CTA both function and share the same booking destination.
7. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the FAQ transition entirely.
8. LCP element is named and ships with explicit dimensions if it's an image.
9. Keyboard-only navigation reaches every interactive element in visual order.
10. No third-party script blocks above-the-fold render.

title: Client Journey Section
our_text:
# Client Journey Section

The what-to-expect section for the S4 kit: the steps from first contact to resolution, stated plainly enough that a prospective client can picture the process before they call. Its job is to lower the anxiety that keeps people from contacting a professional in the first place. Done means a first-time visitor can read the section in under a minute and know what happens after they submit the contact form.

## Structure

1. Section heading and one-line framing ("What to expect").
2. Ordered steps (3–6), each with a short title, a one-sentence description, and what the client provides.
3. Optional timeframe or cost note per step.
4. Closing CTA back to contact or booking.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Mobile and tablet: steps stack as a single-column numbered list, with a connecting line running vertically behind the numbers. Desktop: a horizontal step row with a connecting line when step count is 4 or fewer; falls back to the vertical stack when step count exceeds 4, rather than compressing text to fit a row. Step order never changes across breakpoints.

## Typography

Section heading: display role, step 3 on a 1.25 modular scale, semibold. Step title: step 1, medium. Step description: step 0 (16px base), regular, 45–65 character line length — shorter than page body prose because steps sit in narrow columns at desktop. Step numbers are decorative; they are never the only signal of order, since DOM text order is the source of truth.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (section background), `--ink` (step titles and descriptions, ≥4.5:1 on `--surface`), `--accent` (step-number badges and the closing CTA, ≥3:1 against `--surface`), `--muted` (the connecting line and any cost/timeframe note, ≥3:1 as a UI element), `--border` (card edges, if steps are rendered as cards rather than a plain list).

## Components

**Step item** — number badge, title, description, optional meta line ("what you provide," cost, or timeframe). States: default only; this is static content with no interaction beyond the closing CTA.

**Closing CTA** — button or link back to contact/booking. States: default, hover, focus-visible, active.

## Content slots

Step count (3–6, client decides). Per step: title (`[3–6 words]`), description (`[1 sentence, ~20 words]`), "what you provide" note (`[optional, 1 short phrase]`), timeframe/cost note (`[optional, e.g. "Free, 30 min"]`). CTA label and destination.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: micro, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, applied only to the closing CTA's hover and focus-visible states. The step list itself carries no motion — no staggered reveal, no scroll-triggered animation. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the CTA's transition entirely.

## Accessibility

Steps are marked up as an ordered list (`<ol>`) so assistive technology announces position and count ("step 2 of 4"), not a sequence of styled `<div>`s. Number badges are `aria-hidden`, since list semantics already carry order. The closing CTA meets the ≥44×44px touch-target minimum and carries a focus-visible outline at ≥3:1 contrast. Heading hierarchy: the section heading is one `<h2>` under the page's `<h1>`; step titles are not separate headings unless the page has no other landmark path to them.

## Performance

No LCP-relevant media in this section — text and, at most, small icons. Any step icons ship as inline SVG rather than an icon font or a separate image request. No webfont-driven layout shift, since step text shares the page's already-loaded font stack. No third-party embeds.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** steps typically read consultation → engagement letter → discovery/work → resolution; a note near the resolution stage states that outcomes are not guaranteed.
- **Financial advisory:** steps read discovery call → plan proposal → onboarding → ongoing review; a note states a proposal is not investment advice until an agreement is signed.
- **Medical:** steps read booking → intake forms → visit → follow-up; the "what you provide" slot names what to bring (ID, insurance card) explicitly.
- **Consulting:** steps read scoping call → proposal → engagement → delivery; this is the vertical with the most latitude to name a defined methodology, if the firm has one.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Steps render as a real ordered list, announced with position and count.
- [ ] Step count is between 3 and 6, with no placeholder steps left in.
- [ ] Desktop horizontal layout falls back to a vertical stack above 4 steps.
- [ ] Closing CTA meets the 44×44px minimum and shows a visible focus ring.
- [ ] No motion is applied to the step list itself, only to the closing CTA.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the CTA's transition.
- [ ] Cost/timeframe notes are marked optional and omit cleanly when absent.
- [ ] The section reads standalone in under a minute of reading time.

title: Provider Profile Page
our_text:
# Provider Profile Page

The template for `/team/{slug}` in the S4 Professional Services Trust & Booking kit. It is often the first page a referred client lands on, arriving from a referral link or a name search rather than the firm's homepage, so it must stand alone: full credentials, focus areas, and a direct path to book, without requiring the visitor to have seen the homepage first. Done means a visitor unfamiliar with the firm can decide "is this the right person" and book a consultation without leaving the page.

## Structure

1. **Provider header** — photo, name, title, credentials line, primary book/call action.
2. **Credentials & admissions** — licences, bar/board certifications, jurisdictions, expiry where relevant.
3. **Focus areas** — practice/specialty tags, each linking back to `/practice/{slug}`.
4. **Education & background** — degrees, institutions, prior experience.
5. **Languages spoken.**
6. **Publications / speaking** — optional, client-supplied; section omits itself when empty.
7. **Booking panel** — consultation types, availability, secondary contact.
8. **Related team members** — optional cross-link back to `/team`.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Mobile: single column, header stacked, booking panel directly after the header. Tablet: two-column header (photo left, identity right), body single column below. Desktop: two-column body — main content left (~65%), booking panel right (~35%), sticky as the visitor scrolls. Photo and header never reflow into the booking panel's column.

## Typography

Provider name: display role, step 4 on a 1.25 modular scale, semibold. Title/credentials line: step 1, medium. Body (bio, education): step 0 (16px base), 60–75 character lines. Section labels (Education, Languages) use the label role: uppercase, letter-spaced, treated as labels not headings in scan order. H1 is the provider name; each section below is an H2.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (page/card background), `--ink` (body text, ≥4.5:1), `--accent` (booking CTA and focus rings, ≥3:1 against surface, ≥4.5:1 as text), `--muted` (credentials line and secondary text, ≥4.5:1), `--border` (dividers and card edges, ≥3:1). No brand colour is named or hardcoded.

## Components

**Provider header** — photo (fixed aspect, `object-fit: cover`, alt text naming person and role), name, credentials line, book CTA. States: photo loading (skeleton, no layout shift), photo missing (initials-avatar fallback).

**Credential list** — label/value rows, real list markup. States: expired credential (flagged inline, never hidden), jurisdiction-limited credential (jurisdiction shown inline, never omitted).

**Booking panel** — consultation-type selector, primary CTA, secondary "call instead" link. States: default, hover, focus-visible, active, loading, no-availability (falls back to a native contact form), error (retry plus a visible phone fallback).

## Content slots

Photo (`[Client-supplied headshot, min 800×800px]`), name and title, credentials line (`[Licence/certification — jurisdiction]` per credential), bio (`[150–250 word bio]`), education (`[Degree, Institution, Year]` × N), languages, publications (`[Title, Publication, Year]`, optional — omit the section rather than show an empty heading).

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: micro, ≤150ms, opacity/transform only, hover and focus-visible feedback only. No page-load animation, no scroll-triggered reveal. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets all transition durations to zero rather than shortening them.

## Accessibility

Photo alt text is descriptive ("Dr. Amara Okafor, board-certified dentist"), not "photo of [name]". Credential list uses real `<ul>`/`<dl>` markup, not styled `<div>`s. Booking CTA is a real `<button>`/`<a>` with a visible focus outline (≥3:1, ≥2px). All targets ≥44×44px. Heading order is strictly sequential. The sticky booking panel never traps keyboard focus and stays reachable via Tab in source order.

## Performance

Named LCP element: the provider photo. Explicit `width`/`height`, `loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"` above the fold; below-fold images lazy-load. No webfont-driven layout shift. The booking widget's third-party script loads after the page is interaction-ready, never render-blocking.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** credentials show bar admissions by state; case-experience mentions carry a "not a guarantee of outcome" note.
- **Financial advisory:** credentials show registrations (Series licences, CFP); a fiduciary-status statement sits near the bio.
- **Medical:** credentials show board certification and licence state; "accepting new patients" and insurance-accepted notes appear near booking.
- **Consulting:** credentials optional or lighter-weight; emphasize sector experience and named engagement types instead.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Page renders standalone with full navigation, not requiring homepage context.
- [ ] Every credential slot shows jurisdiction or expiry where applicable.
- [ ] Booking panel is visible or one scroll away at every breakpoint.
- [ ] Photo has explicit dimensions and produces no layout shift on load.
- [ ] All interactive elements are reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
- [ ] Focus-visible ring meets 3:1 contrast on every interactive element.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets transitions to zero duration.
- [ ] No fabricated bio, credential, or publication content appears in placeholders.
- [ ] Publications section omits cleanly when empty, with no dangling heading.

title: Professional Services Homepage Skeleton
our_text:
# Professional Services Homepage Skeleton

The reference homepage for the S4 kit: a professional services firm at SMB scale (law, financial advisory, medical or dental practice, consulting) that must read as credible and calm, not promotional. Done means a working `/` route with every region below present, a shared header and footer every other S4 page reuses unmodified, and the route map wired even where pages are stubs.

## Structure

1. **Header** — identity, primary nav, phone, one booking CTA. Persistent across all routes.
2. **Hero** — practice promise, immediate action, one credibility marker.
3. **Credentials & licensure band** — licences, bar admissions, board certifications, memberships.
4. **Practice areas grid** — the firm's service lines, each linking to its own landing page.
5. **Team preview** — 3–4 featured providers linking to the full directory.
6. **Client journey (process)** — the steps from first contact to resolution.
7. **Testimonials with compliance notes** — endorsements handled per vertical rules, or a stated absence where the vertical forbids them.
8. **Booking & contact block** — consultation entry point plus a secure alternative to email.
9. **Footer** — NAP, licensing jurisdiction, legal links, compliance disclaimer slot.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: mobile `<640px`, tablet `640–1024px`, desktop `>1024px`. Single column at mobile. Credentials band and practice-areas grid move 1 → 2 → 3–4 columns across the breakpoints. Team preview scrolls horizontally on mobile, grids from tablet up. The client-journey list stays single-column and vertical always — a sequence, not a grid. Header nav collapses behind a disclosure control below 1024px; phone and CTA never collapse.

## Typography

Modular scale, 1.25 ratio, base 16px. Roles: display (hero promise, H1), heading (section titles, H2–H3), body (paragraphs, 16–18px), label (nav, form labels, captions). Body line length 45–75 characters. Headings 600–700 weight, body 400, labels 500. One H1 per page, no skipped heading levels.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (background), `--ink` (primary text, ≥4.5:1), `--accent` (CTAs/links, ≥3:1 as a UI boundary, ≥4.5:1 as text), `--muted` (secondary text/captions, ≥4.5:1), `--border` (dividers and input outlines, ≥3:1). No colour is hardcoded or named; the client's palette fills these tokens.

## Components

**Header** — logo (links to `/`), nav (`Practice Areas`, `Team`, `Resources`, `Contact`), phone (`tel:` link, always visible), primary CTA `Book a Consultation` (links to `/booking`). States: default, hover, focus-visible on every link and CTA, active nav item marked by more than colour. Mobile nav collapses behind a labelled disclosure button; phone and CTA stay visible.

**Footer** — name, address, phone (identical to the header), licensing jurisdiction line, links (`Practice Areas`, `Team`, `Privacy Policy`, `Accessibility Statement`, `Terms`), compliance disclaimer slot, copyright.

## Content slots
