Practice name, tagline (1 sentence), phone, address, hours, 3–20 practice areas with 1-line descriptions, 3–60 provider entries, compliance disclaimer text (client's counsel supplies wording), licensing jurisdiction statement. Every slot marked `[Client-supplied: <what>]`; placeholders read as obviously fake, e.g. `[Practice name]`, never an invented firm name.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid. Only hover/focus/active feedback, ≤150ms, opacity or transform only. No scroll-triggered animation, parallax, WebGL, or autoplay video. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the ≤150ms transitions rather than shortening them.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA. Visible keyboard focus ring on every interactive element (≥3:1 against adjacent colours). Logical heading order, one H1 per page. Touch targets ≥44×44px. Skip-to-content link is the first focusable element. Keyboard path: skip link → header nav → hero CTA → each section in DOM order → footer. Nav disclosure button carries `aria-expanded`.

## Performance

LCP element is the hero heading or hero image, whichever renders first — name it per build. Images ship with explicit `width`/`height` and `loading="lazy"` except the LCP candidate (`fetchpriority="high"`). Webfonts use `font-display: swap` with matched fallback metrics. No third-party embed loads render-blocking above the fold.

## Vertical adaptation

Not applicable at the skeleton level — this defines the shared shape. Vertical-specific adaptation lives in the four named full-page prompts and layers onto this skeleton without duplicating it here.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] All nine regions are present in order on `/`.
- [ ] Header and footer markup is identical (data aside) across every route.
- [ ] Routes `/`, `/practice-areas`, `/practice/{slug}`, `/team`, `/team/{slug}`, `/booking`, `/intake`, `/resources`, `/contact`, `/thank-you` all resolve.
- [ ] Phone and address match exactly between header, footer, and any schema markup.
- [ ] Every colour reference in code is a `--token`, none a literal hex/rgb value.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass reaches every interactive element in order with a visible focus ring.
- [ ] No motion exceeds 150ms or animates a property other than opacity/transform.
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes all transitions when tested.
- [ ] Named LCP element loads with `fetchpriority="high"`.

title: Provider Directory
our_text:
# Provider Directory

A filterable directory of the firm's attorneys, advisors or clinicians, built to work
identically for a four-person practice and a sixty-person one. "Done" means a visitor
can filter to the right professional by practice area, location or language, keep
their place while doing it, and reach a booking or profile action without a dead end.

## Structure

1. Directory heading and short intro line (what this page is, one sentence).
2. Filter controls — practice area, location, language; visible, not hidden in a
   drawer at desktop width.
3. Result count — live, states how many providers match the current filters.
4. Provider grid — one card per person, filtered result set.
5. Empty state — shown when filters match no one.
6. Pagination or "load more" — only above a stated provider count (see Layout).

## Layout & responsive

- Mobile (< 640px): single column cards; filters collapse into a single "Filter"
  button opening a full-screen panel, closable without losing selections.
- Tablet (640–1024px): two-column cards; filters shown inline as a row of selects.
- Desktop (≥ 1024px): three-column cards; filters remain a visible inline row above
  the grid, never a hidden drawer at this width.
- Below 20 providers: no pagination, full filtered list renders.
- 20+ providers: paginate at 24 per page, or use "load more" that appends without a
  full page reload — either way, the filter state and scroll position persist.
- Filter controls do not reflow into a different control type across breakpoints
  (always selects/checkboxes, never a select on mobile and a slider on desktop).

## Typography

- Directory heading: display role, step 4.
- Provider name: step 2, semibold.
- Credentials line (e.g. "JD, Bar No. 12345" or "CFP®"): label role, step 0.
- Focus area line: body role, step 0, 1 line, clamped with no silent truncation.
- Filter labels: label role, step 0, always visible (not placeholder-only).

## Colour & tokens

- `--surface`: card and filter-bar background.
- `--ink`: name and credentials text, 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
- `--muted`: focus-area line and result count, 4.5:1 against `--surface`.
- `--accent`: active filter chip and primary card action, 3:1 against `--surface`.
- `--border`: card border and filter control border, 3:1 against `--surface`.

## Components

**Filter bar**
- Structure: one control per filter dimension (practice area, location, language),
  each a native `<select>` or checkbox group; a visible "Clear filters" action when
  any filter is active.
- Props/content slots: filter options are derived from actual team data — never a
  static list that can drift out of sync with who's actually on the team.
- States: default, focus-visible per control, active-filter (chip or highlighted
  select), disabled dimension (e.g. language filter hidden entirely if the firm has
  none to report — omit, don't show an empty control).

**Provider card**
- Structure: photo, name, credentials line, one focus-area line, primary action
  (Book or View Profile), linking to `/team/{slug}`.
- Content slots: `name`, `credentials`, `focus_line` (≤100 characters), `photo`,
  `practice_areas` (for filtering), `location`, `languages` (optional).
- States: default, hover (border/accent shift ≤150ms), focus-visible, active,
  loading (skeleton, only during a client-side filter re-render), and a match/no-match
  state driven by the current filters.

**Empty state**
- Structure: one line stating no providers match, plus a "Clear filters" action.
- No invented "try these providers instead" suggestion.

## Content slots

- `providers[]` — each with `name`, `credentials`, `photo`, `focus_line`,
  `practice_areas[]`, `location`, `languages[]` (optional), `slug`.
- Filter option lists are generated from this data, not authored separately.
- No provider appears without firm-supplied credentials — never infer a licence or
  admission from a job title.

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: avoid, per S4. Filtering re-renders the grid without an animated
reflow — cards appear/disappear on a ≤150ms opacity transition at most, no layout
animation, no stagger effect. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the opacity
transition and swaps the result set instantly. No motion on the filter bar itself
beyond focus-visible feedback.

## Accessibility

- Filter changes update a live region (`aria-live="polite"`) announcing the new
  result count, so screen-reader users hear the effect of their filter choice.
- Filtering is keyboard-operable end to end via native selects and a reachable
  "Clear filters" control.
- Filtering must not move keyboard focus away from the filter bar or reset scroll
  position — the user's place in the page is preserved after every filter change.
- Each provider card is a single link with an accessible name combining name and
  credentials, not name alone (two "Jane Smith" entries must remain distinguishable).
- Touch targets ≥44×44px for filter controls and card actions.
- Colour contrast: 4.5:1 body/credential text, 3:1 filter control borders and focus
  rings.

## Performance

- LCP element is the directory heading, not a provider photo — first-page provider
  photos ship with explicit `width`/`height` and standard `loading="lazy"` except the
  first row, which may use `loading="eager"`.
- Full provider list renders server-side on first load; filtering is a client
  component operating on already-fetched data (no re-fetch per filter change) unless
  the roster exceeds a size where server-side filtering is documented as the
  alternative.
- No layout shift when the result count updates — reserve space for the count line.

## Vertical adaptation

- **Law:** credentials show bar admissions by jurisdiction; area filter maps to
  legal specialisms, never implies certification the state bar doesn't recognize.
- **Financial advisory:** credentials show designations (CFP®, CFA) and registration
  status; location filter matters for state-specific licensing.
- **Medical/dental:** credentials show board certification; language spoken matters
  more here — surface it prominently, not as a secondary filter.
- **Consulting:** "credentials" may be prior-firm experience, not a licence — label
  the field as experience, honestly.

## Acceptance checks

1. Directory renders correctly with 4 providers and with 60 providers.
2. Filter options are generated from actual provider data, never hardcoded.
3. Filtering updates the result count and announces it via a live region.
4. Filtering does not shift keyboard focus or reset scroll position.
5. Empty state appears when filters match no provider, with a working clear action.
6. Every provider card has a distinguishing accessible name (name + credentials).
7. Pagination or "load more" appears only at 20+ providers, and preserves filters.
8. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the card-transition animation entirely.
9. Touch targets for filter controls and card actions are ≥44×44px.
10. No credential or language is shown that isn't present in the provider's data.

title: Testimonials with Compliance Handling
our_text:
# Testimonials with Compliance Handling

This component handles client and patient endorsements for regulated professional-services verticals, where a generic five-star carousel can create real regulatory exposure. Its job is to display legitimate social proof without making a claim the regulator forbids. Done means it defaults to the most restrictive posture, requires the firm to confirm which rule applies, and never implies a guaranteed outcome. **This is build guidance, not legal advice.** The firm's own compliance counsel, or its bar/regulator liaison, is the authority on what its jurisdiction permits, and must sign off before launch.

## Structure

1. Section heading, framed as "What clients say" rather than promotional language.
2. Testimonial cards — or a single testimonial, where volume itself reads as promotional.
3. Required disclaimer line, adjacent to the testimonials, not buried in a footer link.
4. Consent/attribution note — name shown only with documented consent, otherwise anonymized.

## Layout & responsive

Breakpoints: `640px`, `1024px`. Mobile: if a carousel is used, one testimonial visible at a time, swipeable, visible pagination dots, no autoplay. Tablet/desktop: prefer a static grid of 2–3 cards over a carousel — a carousel implies curation and rotation some verticals restrict. Disclaimer text never scrolls independently of the testimonials it governs.

## Typography

Quote: body role, step 1 on a 1.25 scale, regular; italicize only if the system already uses italics for quotes elsewhere. Attribution: step 0, medium, smaller than the quote. Disclaimer: step −1 (12px minimum) — never at lower contrast than the 4.5:1 body requirement; small, low-contrast disclaimer text is a compliance failure, not a style choice.

## Colour & tokens

`--surface` (card background), `--ink` (quote text, ≥4.5:1), `--muted` (attribution/disclaimer, ≥4.5:1 — no exemption from body contrast), `--accent` (sparingly, e.g. a quotation-mark glyph), `--border` (card edges).

## Components

**Testimonial card** — quote, attribution (name/initials or "Anonymous client"), optional date. States: default, and "withdrawn" — if a client revokes consent, the firm must remove one card without redeploying.

**Disclaimer block** — static text in normal reading flow, never a tooltip or modal, always visible whenever testimonials are present.

## Content slots

Quote (`[Client testimonial — 2 sentences max, verbatim, documented consent on file]`), attribution (`[First name + last initial, or "Anonymous," per consent on file]`), date (`[Month, Year]`, optional), disclaimer copy (drafted/approved by the firm's compliance counsel, never invented by the build team).

## Interaction & motion

Motion budget: static — no motion by default. A carousel, if used, advances manually only: no autoplay, no autorotate — autoplay repeats claims on a cadence that reads as advertising rotation in some jurisdictions. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables any carousel transition entirely.

## Accessibility

Quotes use `<blockquote>` with `<cite>` for attribution. If a carousel is used: pagination is keyboard-operable, slides announce via `aria-live="polite"` only on manual advance, and a "view all" list alternative exists. Disclaimer text meets the same 4.5:1 contrast as body copy.

## Performance

No LCP-relevant media — text-only component. Weigh any carousel library against the "no heavy dependencies" rule; a CSS-only scroll-snap approach is preferred over a full carousel package.

## Vertical adaptation — per-vertical rules (build guidance, not legal advice)

- **Law:** many state bar rules restrict or prohibit testimonials about matter outcomes, and some require a disclaimer on every page one appears ("results do not guarantee a similar outcome"). Default: hide testimonials until the firm confirms its state bar permits them; render the outcome disclaimer inline with every testimonial, not in a global footer.
- **Financial advisory:** SEC/FINRA marketing rules treat testimonials as advertising subject to specific disclosure — who was compensated, whether the client is representative, and a prominent disclosure statement. Default: never show a testimonial referencing investment performance or returns; general service-quality testimonials only, with the disclosure block always rendered, never optional.
- **Medical:** patient testimonials risk privacy exposure (identifying a patient without documented, HIPAA-compliant authorization) and false-guarantee claims. Default: no identifying detail beyond first-name-and-initial with a signed release on file, no testimonial naming a diagnosis or outcome, no photo without separate documented consent.
- **Consulting:** least restricted — named testimonials with logos are generally permitted, but still require the client's active sign-off on exact wording, and any cited metric (e.g., "reduced costs 30%") must be one the client has agreed to publish, never authored by the agency.
- **All verticals:** a starting posture for the build, not a compliance ruling. Before launch, the firm's compliance counsel confirms which rule set applies and approves the actual disclaimer copy used.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Component defaults to a hidden or restrictive state until the firm confirms its vertical's rule.
- [ ] Disclaimer renders inline with testimonials, never only in a footer or modal.
- [ ] Disclaimer text meets the same 4.5:1 contrast as body copy.
- [ ] No autoplay or autorotate exists on any carousel implementation.
- [ ] Attribution never shows a full name without documented consent noted in the content-slot instructions.
- [ ] A single testimonial can be removed for consent withdrawal without redeploying the section.
- [ ] No fabricated quote, statistic, or outcome claim appears in placeholder content.
- [ ] The section states plainly that this is build guidance, not legal advice, and requires the firm's compliance counsel to sign off before launch.
